#### VTX-F-002 — validateMenuItem for Export WAV and Export M4A each runs WAVExportCoordinator.makePlan (full editable-song build, whole-song traversal, Fxx timing planning, WAV

- **ID:** VTX-F-002 (`F-concurrency-stale:menu-validation-builds-full-export-plan`)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** efficiency-main-thread
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** validateMenuItem for Export WAV and Export M4A each runs WAVExportCoordinator.makePlan (full editable-song build, whole-song traversal, Fxx timing planning, WAV layout validation) on the main thread on every menu validation pass, and beginExport then recomputes the plan twice more.

**Evidence:** AppDelegate.swift:230-233 -> WAVExportCoordinator.unavailableReason (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:338-361, makePlan at :354); M4AExportCoordinator.swift:286-292 delegates to the same, so File-menu validation plans twice; beginExport (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:363-387) calls unavailableReason (plan 1) then makePlan again (plan 2); EditablePlaybackSongBuilder.build (BlankTrackerDocument.swift:2343-2410) rebuilds every pattern row/cell per call; export items have no key equivalents (ApplicationMenuBuilder.swift:83,93-94) so cost is bounded to menu opens.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Menu validation is cheap, near-constant-time main-thread work.

**Why it matters:** Cost scales with song size (patterns x rows x channels plus full traversal/timing planning). For large compositions this becomes repeated main-thread jank on every File menu open, and triple plan computation at export start; the dedicated WAVExportPlanPerformanceDiagnostics phases show this work is considered nontrivial.

**Reproduction / proof:** Proposed: open the File menu repeatedly with a 256-pattern, 32-channel synthetic document while measuring validateMenuItem latency (two full plans per open); compare against a cheap structural check.

**Existing mitigation:** Current fixtures and small alpha songs plan in milliseconds; no key equivalents means no per-keystroke validation.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Make unavailableReason use a cheap structural check (document/song present, playback inactive) for menu validation and defer full plan construction to beginExport; reuse the plan computed by the availability check instead of recomputing.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test asserting canExport does not invoke the song builder (counter hook), plus a perf smoke on a large synthetic document.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding confirmed as described, with one correction: the WAV/M4A menu items live in the File > Export Audio submenu (parent item has nil action), so under AppKit auto-enablement the two full-plan validations fire when the Export Audio submenu is displayed (hover), not on every top-level File-menu open. Everything else traced exactly: canExport -> unavailableReason -> full makePlan (discarded); M4A delegates to the same WAV path so one validation pass plans twice; beginExport computes the plan twice more (unavailableReason plan discarded at WAVExportCoordinator.swift:365, makePlan again at :371); no caching exists in the coordinator; the only canExport callers are the two validateMenuItem cases. Cost per plan is O(patterns x rows x channels) song rebuild for editable documents plus a whole-song traversal bounded by traversalRowLimit at up to 1,000,000 synthetic rows (PlaybackSongAdapter+Traversal.swift:688-701) and a per-cell Fxx timing scan — so a valid loop-heavy (E6x) or long document can make each discarded validation plan cost tens of millions of cell visits synchronously on the main thread. Mitigations confirmed: no key equivalents on WAV/M4A items (no per-keystroke validation), loadedReadOnly contexts skip the song rebuild (reuse playbackEngine.song), and current alpha-scale songs plan in milliseconds. Severity MEDIUM is fair (borderline LOW): pure efficiency debt, no correctness impact, not alpha-blocking, but real scheduled-work material given the redundant triple plan at export start and unbounded-ish scaling with song size during menu tracking. Fix direction: cheap structural check for validateMenuItem, single plan computation in beginExport.

#### VTX-F-003 — There is no applicationShouldTerminate guard for in-flight exports; Cmd+Q mid-export kills the render thread and permanently orphans hidden UUID-named temp file

- **ID:** VTX-F-003 (`F-concurrency-stale:quit-during-export-orphans-temp-files`)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** lifecycle-cleanup
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 2 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** There is no applicationShouldTerminate guard for in-flight exports; Cmd+Q mid-export kills the render thread and permanently orphans hidden UUID-named temp files (up to ~800 MB raw plus ~800 MB final for maximum-length renders) in the user-chosen destination directory, with no cleanup sweep on any later launch.

**Evidence:** AppDelegate.swift has no applicationShouldTerminate/applicationWillTerminate (only applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed at :216-218). Temp names include a fresh UUID per export: WAVExportCoordinator.swift:771-775 and M4AExportCoordinator.swift:486-489, so the pre-run removeItem calls (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:535-536, M4AExportCoordinator.swift:334-335) can never reclaim a prior run's orphans; grep confirms no other non-test code references the .vtx-export- prefix.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Export temp files never outlive the export operation.

**Why it matters:** maximumFrameCount is 100,000,000 frames (WAVExportCoordinatorTests.swift:18-19); at stereo float32 that is ~800 MB per temp file, hidden (dot-prefixed) in a user directory. A quit or crash mid-export silently aborts the export and leaks the space with no visible artifact.

**Reproduction / proof:** Start a long WAV export, press Cmd+Q while the rendering stage is active, relaunch, then ls -a the destination directory: .name.wav.vtx-export-render-UUID.tmp remains and is never removed by any later run.

**Existing mitigation:** The destination file itself is safe (atomic replace happens only at the end); completion, failure, and cancellation paths all clean temps (verified by tests at WAVExportCoordinatorTests.swift:283-405, 1093-1166).

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Implement applicationShouldTerminate to cancel the token and wait briefly (or prompt) when audioExportProgressSheet != nil; optionally sweep stale .vtx-export-* siblings of the destination before starting a new export.

**Recommended timing:** next milestone

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Test that a terminate request during an active export cancels the token and lets export() clean temps before termination proceeds.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding confirmed exactly as reported; severity MEDIUM and reachability agree with the reporter. Traced refutation attempts all failed: (a) no applicationShouldTerminate/applicationWillTerminate exists anywhere in Swift sources (only applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed at AppDelegate.swift:216-218), so Cmd+Q takes the default terminateNow path; (b) the export runs on DispatchQueue.global (AppDelegate.swift:573, 627) with only a window-modal NSPanel sheet (parent.beginSheet at AppDelegate.swift:3248-3251, no runModal), so quit is not blocked and process exit kills the render before the catch-path cleanups (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:709-725) or the M4A defer (M4AExportCoordinator.swift:336-339) run; (c) temp names embed a fresh UUID per call (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:771-775, M4AExportCoordinator.swift:486-489), so the pre-run removeItem calls (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:535-536, M4AExportCoordinator.swift:334-335) can never reclaim a prior run's orphans, and grep confirms no other non-test code references '.vtx-export-' (no launch sweep). Size math verified from production code, not just tests: AudioExportRenderLimits.maximumFrameCount = 100_000_000 (SoftwareMixer.swift:420-422, wired via productWAVExport SoftwareMixer.swift:439 and WAVExportCoordinator.swift:132/324/541), defaultChannelCount = 2 (SoftwareMixer.swift:120), float32 => 800,000,000 bytes per temp; raw+final temps coexist during the non-unity headroom pass (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:636-658). Aggravating detail the reporter missed: the M4A path nests a full WAV export targeting pcmTempURL (M4AExportCoordinator.swift:341-351), so a mid-export quit can orphan the pcm WAV temp plus the nested raw/final temps (~2.4 GB worst case). Mitigating claims also verified: destination file is only touched via atomic replace at the end (WAVExportCoordinator.swift:674), and single-run completion/failure/cancel paths do clean temps. MEDIUM is right: no destination corruption or document data loss, but a supported workflow silently aborts the export and permanently leaks hidden multi-hundred-MB files in a user directory. Fix direction (not a protected boundary): implement applicationShouldTerminate to cancel-and-wait or prompt during an active export, and/or a launch/pre-export sweep for stale '.vtx-export-*' siblings of the chosen destination.
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding confirmed as described, at the reporter's severity. WAV and M4A export coordinators create hidden UUID-named temp files in the user-chosen destination directory; cleanup exists only on in-process success/failure/cancel paths (catch blocks and a defer), so crash or force-quit mid-export orphans them permanently. The "pre-clean" of freshly generated UUID paths is provably a no-op, and grep across the repo shows no other code references the vtx-export- prefix — no startup or subsequent-export sweep. The app is not sandboxed (no entitlements file, no CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS in project.pbxproj), so sibling writes in the destination directory succeed. Two amplifiers the reporter understated slightly: (a) M4A export nests a WAV export targeting its own pcm temp, so a single M4A crash can orphan multiple large files (pcm temp + nested render temp + encoded temp); (b) the size ceiling is ~800 MB per temp (100,000,000 frames x stereo x 4-byte Float32 at 48 kHz, SoftwareMixer.swift:421). Severity LOW is right: precondition is abnormal termination, impact is hidden disk consumption only, no user-content corruption; the beside-destination temp placement itself is a sound same-volume atomic-rename design. Mitigation options: purpose-stable temp names (overwrite/reclaim on next export to same destination) or a prefix-matching sweep of the destination directory before export.

**Independently rediscovered by:** `H-path-export-security:crash-orphaned-hidden-temp-files-in-destination-dir` (LOW) — merged into this finding; concurrence across independent auditors raises confidence.

#### VTX-J-002 — Edit > Clear Song Data on a loaded module is a second loaded-to-editable conversion route whose validation has diverged from Make Editable Copy: it copies playb

- **ID:** VTX-J-002 (`J-architecture-drift:clear-song-data-bypasses-editable-copy-boundary`)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** diverged-duplicate-validation
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** Edit > Clear Song Data on a loaded module is a second loaded-to-editable conversion route whose validation has diverged from Make Editable Copy: it copies playbackSong.instrumentsByIndex verbatim with no linear-frequency-table check, no sparse-slot provenance boundary, no map/sample-index bounds, and no EditableXMWriter dry-run.

**Evidence:** AppDelegate.swift:1605-1641 clearSongData loaded branch gated only by loadedModuleCanMakeEditableCopy() (3147-3156: checks only nonempty PCM) and BlankTrackerDocument.makeEditableCopyClearingSongData (BlankTrackerDocument.swift:889-922: guard is hasUsableInstrumentSamplePalette only; palette = playbackSong.instrumentsByIndex verbatim). Contrast LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator.swift:97-157 (requires usesLinearFrequencyTable, writer dry-run at 152) and 161-202 matchesLoadedSampleCopyBoundary (unique bounded sample indices, 96-entry bounded map, canonical provenance for gaps). PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:140 reads sampleCount as raw LE16 (not clamped to 16) and 248-261 readNoteSampleMap returns raw 0-255 bytes, so out-of-boundary palettes are loadable. docs/design/editable-document-save-export-model.md:62,67-71 promises the bridge preserves a "safely represented" palette.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** canonical editable keymap-presence and bounded sparse sample-identity invariants hold for every supported entry into editable state; every editable document is exportable through the supported XM writer

**Why it matters:** The Sample Lifecycle Alpha invested heavily in one guarded loaded-to-editable boundary (writer dry-run + provenance span check), but the older Clear Song Data bridge skips all of it. A loadable XM with >16 sample headers, map bytes >=16, or a samples-with-nil-map instrument enters the editable palette as noncanonical state: sample-lifecycle transactions then silently refuse (state D) and Export XM throws (unsupportedSampleIndexOrder / unsupportedNoteSampleMap per EditableXMWriter.swift:286-329), leaving the user with an editable composition that cannot export. Amiga-table XMs (common) are blocked from Make Editable Copy but pass Clear Song Data and are silently re-typed as linear-table documents (EditablePlaybackSongBuilder, BlankTrackerDocument.swift:2378 usesLinearFrequencyTable: true).

**Reproduction / proof:** Open an XM whose instrument declares 17 sample headers with payloads (or 96-note map bytes >= 16) — PlaybackSongBuilder loads it; Edit > Clear Song Data (enabled because PCM exists); resulting editable document holds sampleIndex 16 / out-of-range map; attempt Export XM -> writer error alert; attempt Move/Swap/Clear Sample -> silently unavailable. Proposed synthetic-fixture test; not executed (build prohibited).

**Existing mitigation:** Well-formed FT2-subset modules produce canonical palettes, so the common path is unaffected; writer validation still prevents emitting malformed XM (failure is an error alert, not corrupt output); lifecycle transactions reject noncanonical state without mutation.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Funnel the Clear Song Data loaded-module branch through the same palette admission used by LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator (matchesLoadedSampleCopyBoundary + writer dry-run on the cleared document), or at minimum replace AppDelegate.loadedModuleCanMakeEditableCopy() with the coordinator's unavailableReason check.

**Recommended timing:** next milestone

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Add coordinator-level tests: synthetic XM with 17 sample headers / map byte 16 / Amiga table -> Clear Song Data either refuses or produces a document that passes EditableXMWriter().data(from:) without throwing.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Confirmed as reported, with one scope correction: the bridge is XM-only (PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:36 guards metadata.type == "XM", so MOD modules never produce playbackEngine.song and Clear Song Data stays unavailable for them). Everything else traced true: the loaded branch of clearSongData converts to editable state through BlankTrackerDocument.makeEditableCopyClearingSongData whose only guard is any-nonempty-PCM, copying playbackSong.instrumentsByIndex verbatim, with no linear-frequency-table check, no sparse-slot provenance/bounds boundary, and no EditableXMWriter dry-run — all of which LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator enforces for Make Editable Copy. PlaybackSongBuilder places no clamp on sampleCount (raw LE16) and returns raw 0-255 noteSampleMap bytes, so noncanonical palettes (sampleIndex >= 16, map bytes >= 16) enter editable state; EditableXMWriter then rejects export (unsupportedSampleIndexOrder at 306, unsupportedNoteSampleMap at 463/471) via a warning alert, and lifecycle mutations silently return nil on bounds guards, leaving a composable-but-unexportable document with Save disabled. Amiga-table XMs pass this bridge and are silently re-typed linear (BlankTrackerDocument.swift:2378) despite Make Editable Copy refusing them, contradicting docs/design/editable-document-save-export-model.md:62,67-71 ('safely represented palette'). Severity MEDIUM is correct: common well-formed FT2-subset path unaffected, no on-disk corruption, no malformed XM emission, but a real validation divergence with a user-visible dead end (work done in the bridged document cannot be exported) reachable from a supported menu command on dirty-but-loadable XMs. Files read fully: LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator.swift, docs section; targeted reads (verified line-by-line) in AppDelegate.swift, BlankTrackerDocument.swift, PlaybackSongBuilder.swift, EditableXMWriter.swift.

**Summary:** Current pattern/order position for editable documents is stored twice — in BlankTrackerDocument (currentPosition/currentPatternIndex) and in AppDelegate mirrors (selectedSongPositionIndex/currentPatternIndex/selectedPatternSelectionIndex) — and the two sets have divergent write paths, so any applyEdit snaps the visible tracker view back to the document's stale position.

**Evidence:** AppDelegate.swift:114-116 (mirror fields), 1801-1814 patternSelectionChanged and 1893-1901 currentSongPositionStepperChanged + 2294-2307 applySongPosition (update mirrors only, never blankDocument), 2228-2245 applyPlaybackPosition (mirrors only); versus 1254-1330 SongOrderEditor selection paths which update the document AND mirrors; 1493-1508 applyEditableDocumentSnapshot overwrites the mirrors from document.currentPosition/currentPatternIndex on every applyEdit (called by EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.swift:319 documentApplyHandler). **Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** ADR 010 whole-document edit/undo funnel: destructive edits share one mutation and refresh boundary with reciprocal undo

**Why it matters:** This is the largest remaining declared-vs-actual gap at the applyEdit boundary. Interleaved workflows are the norm in this milestone (enter notes, tweak a sample, enter more notes): each note entry silently wipes undo for the preceding Clear Sample/Reorder Samples/import edits, making the advertised sample-lifecycle undo guarantees fragile in real use. Two mutation idioms in the same controller also invite new features to copy the wrong one.

**Reproduction / proof:** File > New; generate sine; Clear Sample (undoable); type one note into the pattern in edit mode; Edit > Undo is now disabled — the Clear Sample snapshot is gone. Straight from code path AppDelegate.swift:2485; not executed (build prohibited).

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Migrate pattern note/keyoff/clear-field entry (possibly coalesced per row) and the Song Order editor operations to labeled applyEdit transactions; retire discardUndoHistory() from those paths.

**Recommended timing:** next milestone

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Existing EditableDocumentEditCoordinatorTests plus new tests asserting note entry and order insert register undo actions and no longer clear history; manual undo-across-interleaved-edits check.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding is real as described, with one correction: the summary's "all Song Order editor mutations" is slightly overstated. The Song Order editor's Clear Pattern action (AppDelegate.swift:1390-1392 -> clearCurrentEditablePatternForEditing 1568-1588) DOES route through applyEdit(label: "Clear Current Pattern") at line 1584 and is therefore undoable; the reporter's own evidence enumeration (new/duplicate/insert/delete/move/step) correctly excluded it. Everything else holds: every mutating pattern keystroke (note, key-off, clear field) and every other Song Order mutation assigns blankDocument directly and calls discardUndoHistory(), wiping the full 20-level sample-lifecycle undo stack. This is a documented deliberate interim state (ADR 010 line 20), so users get a missing undo, never a wrong one — no data corruption, no incorrect XM, no crash, so not HIGH/BLOCKER. But it is a genuine declared-vs-actual gap against ADR 012 line 59's blanket statement, it degrades the milestone's advertised undo guarantees in the most common interleaved workflow (enter notes between sample edits), and the coexistence of two mutation idioms in the same controller is real copy-the-wrong-pattern risk. MEDIUM severity, supported-user-workflow reachability, agreeing with the reporter. Repro logic verified statically end-to-end (guards, mutation, discard, menu validation); not executed because builds were prohibited, but no conditional in the path depends on runtime state beyond the stated setup.

The structural claim is nonetheless real and slightly stronger than reported: there are three precedence conventions, not two — qualified contexts (500-515, 518, 1486-1491) effectively favor loadedReadOnly when both set; unqualified editor/control-panel readers (838, 930, 2988) favor blankDocument; and displayedMetadata at line 153 (loadedMetadata ?? blankDocument?.metadata) explicitly favors loadedMetadata. The pinned-gutter divider x-position (dividerX/gutterWidth on TrackerChromeOverlayView and TrackerDividerUnderlayView) is derived from string measurements in a locally constructed font (2938-2944) that must match the body-render font at 2393 and the gutter-draw font at TrackerEditorView.swift:276; only the coincidence of six ofSize:13 literals across two files preserves alignment. #### VTX-M-001 — Holding a tracker note key in the Instrument Editor and moving focus into the NAME field (Tab or click) before releasing swallows the keyUp because the routing

- **ID:** VTX-M-001 (`M-ui-appkit:audition-keyup-swallowed-on-text-focus-stuck-note`)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Confidence:** Medium
- **Category:** audition-routing
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** Holding a tracker note key in the Instrument Editor and moving focus into the NAME field (Tab or click) before releasing swallows the keyUp because the routing policy rejects events when firstResponder is a text editor, leaving a sustained (looping-sample) audition preview sounding with no release.

**Evidence:** InstrumentEditorWindowController.swift: InstrumentEditorNoteAuditionRoutingPolicy.action lines 598-624 guards `!isTextEditingResponder(firstResponder)` for BOTH keyDown and keyUp; InstrumentEditorPanel.sendEvent lines 660-674 then passes the unrouted keyUp to the field editor; Tab reaches the NAME field via the key-view loop wired at lines 1822-1823 (contentView.nextKeyView = field) and Tab is a protected key (line 592) so it moves focus mid-hold. No firstResponder-change hook cancels previews (only windowDidResignKey/windowWillClose do, lines 1492-1530). Preview release depends on the keyUp handler (AppDelegate handleInstrumentEditorNoteAuditionKeyUp); EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink.swift release machinery (lines ~373-455) sustains looped preview voices until an explicit release/cancel.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Every accepted note-on audition must have a guaranteed note-off/cancel path across focus transitions within the same key window.

**Why it matters:** A looped sample keeps sounding while the user types an instrument name; nothing in-window stops it until the user presses another note key after leaving the field, deactivates the window, or closes it. It is an audio stuck-note bug in the flagship audition path.

**Reproduction / proof:** Editable document with a forward-looped sample mapped; in the Instrument Editor press and hold 'z' (note sounds), press Tab while holding (focus enters NAME field), release 'z': keyUp is not routed (policy guard), preview continues sounding while editing the name.

**Existing mitigation:** windowDidResignKey and window close cancel previews; starting any new preview replaces the stuck one; non-looped samples end naturally, bounding impact for one-shot samples.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Cancel the active computer-key audition when first responder transitions into a text-editing responder (observe NSWindow first-responder changes or hook the name field's editing-begin and invoke noteAuditionCancelHandler), or route keyUp for tracker keys even when a text responder is focused (keyUp cannot insert text).

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Controller-level test: route keyDown with contentView responder, move focus to the name field editor, send keyUp with NSTextView responder, assert the previewer's active token is cleared (currently it is not).

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Confirmed as described. The routing policy's isTextEditingResponder guard applies identically to keyDown and keyUp, so a note keyUp delivered while the NAME field's field editor is firstResponder is never routed to handleInstrumentEditorNoteAuditionKeyUp, and no other code path stops a preview on in-window focus change (no textDidBeginEditing/controlTextDidBeginEditing handlers, no firstResponder observers, no NSEvent monitors anywhere in the app — verified by grep). The sink sustains a looped voice until an explicit release/cancel generation, so a forward-looped sample keeps sounding while the user types. Corrections to the report: Tab keyCode 48 is at InstrumentEditorWindowController.swift:591 (reporter said 592); the Tab leg depends on default NSWindow key-view-loop handling (no keyDown override exists on the content view, so the event does bubble to the window), but the mouse-click-into-field variant of the repro is fully code-traced and independent of Tab semantics. Reporter's mitigations verified: next noteOn retires the stuck voice (sink render loop lines 429-434), windowDidResignKey/windowWillClose cancel, one-shot samples end naturally. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: audible stuck-note in the flagship audition path within a supported editable-document workflow, but transient, easily recoverable, no state/data corruption, does not block alpha. Fix direction (not a rewrite of protected boundaries): route keyUp regardless of text-editing firstResponder (release-only bypass), or cancel active preview on firstResponder change into a text editor. Note: on-screen keyboard mouse audition (.instrumentEditorKeyboard identity) is unaffected; only physical-key auditions are exposed. I did not build or run the app (read-only audit constraint), so the repro is code-traced, not executed; the only non-repo dependency is documented AppKit focus/field-editor behavior.

#### VTX-M-003 — If the Song/Order editor is open when playback starts, its refresh is skipped by SongOrderEditorRefreshPolicy for the entire playback session, so all mutation/n

- **ID:** VTX-M-003 (`M-ui-appkit:song-order-stale-enabled-controls-during-playback`)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** ui-gating
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** If the Song/Order editor is open when playback starts, its refresh is skipped by SongOrderEditorRefreshPolicy for the entire playback session, so all mutation/navigation buttons remain visually enabled (with active tooltips) but silently no-op because AppDelegate handlers guard on isPlaybackActive.

**Evidence:** SongOrderEditorWindowController.swift lines 673-678 (shouldRefresh requires !isPlaybackActive); AppDelegate.swift lines 1542-1551 (refreshSongOrderEditor is the only refresh path and is policy-gated), lines 1525-1531 (currentSongOrderEditorDisplayState computes isOrderMutationEnabled: !isPlaying, but that state can never reach an already-visible window while playing), lines 1924-1931 and 2091-2092 (playbackEngine.play immediately followed by syncControlPanelView, at which point refresh is already skipped). Handlers guard correctly: AppDelegate.swift lines 1394-1483 and 1254-1256. Content view guards use the stale displayState: SongOrderEditorWindowController.swift lines 887-972. Contrast: the Instrument Editor refreshes unconditionally in syncControlPanelView's defer (AppDelegate.swift lines 2982-2986) and disables its controls via isPlaybackActive.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Playing/read-only gating must be reflected at the UI layer: controls that cannot act should render disabled.

**Why it matters:** Users get enabled-looking CLEAR SONG / DELETE / INSERT buttons during playback that do nothing with no feedback; the panel also shows a stale order highlight. The model is protected (no corruption), but the affordance dishonesty is inconsistent with the Instrument and Sample editors which disable during playback.

**Reproduction / proof:** New editable document, open Song / Order (buttons enabled), start playback from the main window, click '+ INSERT' or 'CLEAR SONG' in the still-open panel: nothing happens, button stays enabled until playback stops and the next refresh runs.

**Existing mitigation:** All AppDelegate mutation handlers and SongOrderEditorNavigation helpers independently guard isPlaybackActive, so no state can be corrupted; opening the panel fresh during playback shows the correctly disabled state.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Push one disabled-state apply to the visible panel at the playback-start transition (e.g., call applyIfVisible with the isPlaybackActive-derived state exactly at play start, or relax shouldRefresh to allow play-start/stop edge applies while still skipping per-row refreshes).

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test: open controller, apply editable enabled state, simulate the play-start refresh, assert mutation buttons render disabled (isEnabled false, target nil) while playback is active.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding confirmed exactly as reported; all cited line ranges verified accurate at commit f0017862. The refresh skip is structural: refreshSongOrderEditor (policy-gated on !isPlaybackActive) is the sole update path for an already-visible Song/Order panel, and every playback-start site calls syncControlPanelView only after playbackEngine.play, so the panel retains its pre-play display state (mutation flags true) for the entire playback session. Buttons render enabled with active tooltips from that stale state; clicks pass the content-view guards but are silently rejected by SongOrderEditorNavigation helpers, all of which I verified guard !isPlaybackActive (model fully protected — no corruption path). Mitigations verified: fresh open during playback applies the correctly disabled state (AppDelegate.swift:775), and stopPressed's syncControlPanelView restores the panel. Severity MEDIUM is right: real UI-gating honesty defect in a supported workflow, inconsistent with the Instrument editor (which refreshes unconditionally with isPlaybackActive in its display state), but transient, self-healing, and with zero data risk — not HIGH; more than LOW because it is user-visible affordance dishonesty, not internal cleanup. Minimal fix direction: push one disabled-state apply on playback start/stop transitions (or exempt a playback-transition refresh from the policy) rather than removing the policy, which likely exists to avoid rebuilding the panel on per-row playback ticks.

**Summary:** Every SongOrderEditorContentView rebuild discards transient view state: the order-list scroll position resets to top whenever the selected order is unchanged, and any app-driven refresh (e.g., octave/edit-mode toggles that call syncControlPanelView) snaps a manually-paged pattern bank back to the auto bank.

**Evidence:** SongOrderEditorWindowController.swift: rebuildShell lines 978-982 removes all subviews; addOrderRowsScrollView lines 1015-1047 creates a fresh NSScrollView at origin 0 with no origin restoration; scrollSelectedOrderRowIfNeeded lines 1049-1067 early-returns when selectedOrderPosition == lastScrolledSelectedOrderPosition, so the new scroll view stays at top. Bank: showBank lines 974-976 mutates only local view state, while AppDelegate.currentSongOrderEditorDisplayState (AppDelegate.swift lines 1525-1541) never passes requestedBankIndex, so refreshSongOrderEditor from any unrelated syncControlPanelView call site (40+ sites) rebuilds with the auto bank. **Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Display-state refreshes should not discard user navigation state (scroll position, bank page) that the refresh did not change.

**Why it matters:** With songs longer than ~12 orders, any pattern op (DUP/CLEAR/+NEW keep the selected order unchanged) or unrelated control-panel sync jumps the order list to the top with the highlighted row off-screen, and browsing bank 2+ of the pattern grid is undone by unrelated refreshes; this makes long-arrangement workflows feel broken.

Separately: page to bank 2 via the bank arrows, then toggle edit mode or change octave in the main window: the bank snaps back to bank 1.

**Existing mitigation:** Selection changes do re-center (scrollSelectedOrderRowIfNeeded), and applyIfVisible no-ops for fully unchanged states, so the reset only occurs on genuine state deltas or bank divergence.

(B) Bank snap-back: showBank stores the requested bank only in local view state; AppDelegate.currentSongOrderEditorDisplayState (1525-1540) never passes requestedBankIndex, so resolvedBankIndex falls back to auto bank; syncControlPanelView (2981-2983) unconditionally defers refreshSongOrderEditor, and unrelated triggers (editModeToggled 1904-1911, octaveSelectionChanged 2006-2009, ~38 other call sites) rebuild with the auto bank whenever the window is visible and playback is stopped (SongOrderEditorRefreshPolicy 674-678). Contrast verified: InstrumentEditorView.apply (1626-1649) captures and restores scroll origins across rebuilds. Reporter's mitigations are accurate: the Equatable guard at line 868 no-ops fully identical states, and genuine selection changes re-center. Impact calibration: the bank snap-back requires >64 patterns (totalBankCount > 1), rare at alpha scale; the scroll reset requires >~12 orders, common. No data loss or corruption — transient view-state only — so MEDIUM (real UX debt in a supported long-arrangement workflow, does not block alpha) is correct; neither HIGH nor LOW.

#### VTX-N-001 — PR/main CI never builds any Release configuration, so Release-only failures (a historically demonstrated class: the Swift 6.3.2 optimizer crash) surface only at

- **ID:** VTX-N-001 (`N-build-ci-release:ci-no-release-config-build`)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** ci-coverage
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** PR/main CI never builds any Release configuration, so Release-only failures (a historically demonstrated class: the Swift 6.3.2 optimizer crash) surface only at tag time in the release workflow.

**Evidence:** .github/workflows/basic-checks.yml lines 20-39 build and test only '-configuration Debug'; lines 40-43 run SwiftPM tests in default debug. No Release build exists anywhere in basic-checks. .github/workflows/release.yml lines 100-133 is the only automated Release build and runs only on tag push/workflow_dispatch. History: commit 98f8b70 ('build: avoid Swift 6.3.2 optimizer crash', PR #375, closed issue #374) added @_optimize(none) to SampleEditorWindowController.swift buildParams because Release-config compilation crashed — found during manual release prep, not by CI.

**Reachability:** build/CI only

**Invariant affected:** AGENTS.md 'CI must remain green on main' implying main is releasable; Release-config compilability is part of releasability but is unverified by CI.

**Why it matters:** A green main can be unreleasable. The failure appears only after the version tag is pushed, when release.yml fails mid-pipeline, leaving a published tag with no release and forcing emergency fixes under release pressure — exactly what happened with the 6.3.2 crash.

**Reproduction / proof:** On a Swift 6.3.2 toolchain, remove '@_optimize(none)' at app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/SampleEditorWindowController.swift:1421 and open a PR: basic-checks passes (Debug only); the breakage first appears in tag-triggered release.yml Release build.

**Existing mitigation:** Maintainer pre-tag checklist (docs/release-notes/v0.3.0-alpha.1.md lines 200-214) manually runs host and universal Release builds before tagging; discipline has held through 6+ releases.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Add one host-arch 'xcodebuild -configuration Release ... CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build' step to basic-checks (at minimum on pushes to main).

**Recommended timing:** next milestone

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** CI run on main shows the Release build step passing; negative test: temporarily reintroduce a Release-only optimizer failure on the affected toolchain and confirm basic-checks goes red before any tag exists.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability build/CI only, confidence High): Every cited element verified against the repo at f0017862. PR/main CI (basic-checks.yml) builds and tests only Debug plus default-configuration SwiftPM tests; the sole automated Release build lives in release.yml and runs only on version-tag push or manual workflow_dispatch. If the tag-triggered Release build fails, the Publish GitHub Release step (release.yml:207-216) never runs, leaving a pushed tag with no release — the exact failure mode. The historical instance is real: issue #374 documents that the v0.3.0-alpha.1 Release build reproducibly crashed the Swift 6.3.2 optimizer while 'Debug builds/tests remain green', discovered during manual release prep; PR #375 / commit 98f8b70 added @_optimize(none) as the workaround, still present at SampleEditorWindowController.swift:1421. Mitigation claim also verified: the maintainer pre-tag checklist (docs/release-notes/v0.3.0-alpha.1.md:200-214) manually runs host and universal Release builds before tagging. One correction/nuance the reporter omitted: release.yml's workflow_dispatch branch (lines 122-133) offers an unsigned Release dry-run buildable without pushing a tag — a manual, not automatic, mitigation lever; it does not weaken the claim that PR/main gating never exercises Release. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: real, historically-demonstrated CI coverage debt, but failure is loud (build break), cannot corrupt state or ship a defective artifact, and is mitigated by documented manual discipline. Cheapest fix would be adding an unsigned ARCHS='arm64 x86_64' Release build step (CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO) to basic-checks, or a scheduled/main-push Release job.

- **ID:** VTX-N-002 (`N-build-ci-release:x86_64-slice-never-tested`)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** release-verification
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** The shipped x86_64 slice of the universal DMG is never executed by any automated test, and the release 'Verify app architecture' step only prints lipo output without asserting both architectures.

**Evidence:** .github/workflows/basic-checks.yml line 11 'runs-on: macos-latest', which resolved to 'Image: macos-26-arm64' in run 33691881432 (log inspected via gh) — all xcodebuild/swift tests execute arm64 only. .github/workflows/release.yml lines 119-120 build ARCHS="arm64 x86_64"; lines 135-138 run only 'lipo -info "$APP_PATH/..."' with no grep/assertion. **Invariant affected:** Shipped binary slices behave as tested; the DSP-heavy C mixer (core/MixerCore/src/vtx_c_mixer.c, compiled directly into the app target per pbxproj lines 612/707) ships to Intel users with zero automated execution on that architecture.

**Reproduction / proof:** Dry run (workflow_dispatch) release.yml with ARCHS reduced to 'arm64': the 'Verify app architecture' step prints 'Non-fat file ... arm64' and succeeds; the single-arch DMG uploads normally.

**Existing mitigation:** Release gate reports record manual 'file' and 'lipo -archs' checks of the universal build; v0.3.0-alpha.1 release run log confirms 'x86_64 arm64' was actually shipped.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Make the verify step assert: lipo -archs output must contain both arm64 and x86_64 (fail otherwise). Optionally add a per-release Rosetta smoke ('arch -x86_64 swift test' or an x86_64 test-bundle run) while Intel remains supported.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Dry-run the workflow with a deliberately single-arch build and confirm the verify step fails; then a normal dry run passes.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity MEDIUM, reachability build/CI only, confidence High): CONFIRMED with corrections. The two concrete claims hold: (1) CI tests run arm64-only (macos-latest resolved to macos-26-arm64, verified in the run log myself), and (2) release.yml's 'Verify app architecture' step only prints lipo -info without asserting both slices — lipo -info succeeds on a non-fat file, so a future edit dropping ARCHS would ship a single-arch DMG to Intel users with the step passing. All cited line numbers are accurate. CORRECTION to the invariant framing: 'zero automated execution on x86_64' is overstated — the maintainer's dev host is an Intel i9-10910 (uname -m = x86_64), and the release-readiness gate ran the full 1,487-test Debug suite plus swift test suites on that host (readiness report lines 116-125), so the x86_64 codegen path of vtx_c_mixer.c and all Swift code does get substantial automated local test execution; the true gap is (a) no CI execution on x86_64 and (b) no automated fat-binary assertion. Also note Release-optimized slices are test-executed for neither arch (tests run Debug), so the 'shipped slice untested' concern applies symmetrically to arm64 Release codegen. Severity MEDIUM stands: README promises Intel support, the only automated guard is non-asserting, and the fix is a one-line 'lipo -archs ... | grep' assertion plus optionally an arch -x86_64 Rosetta smoke test; mitigated by manual gate records and the verified-fat v0.3.0-alpha.1 shipped binary. Reachability corrected from 'supported user workflow' to 'build/CI only': the defect lives entirely in the release pipeline; its blast radius would reach Intel end users only if a regression were introduced, but no current user workflow exercises the defect.

#### VTX-A1-003 — The XM instrument loader imposes no 16-slot bound on declared sample count or note-map byte values, so a malformed XM can carry samples with sampleIndex >= 16 a

- **ID:** VTX-A1-003 (`A1-lifecycle-model:parser-admits-out-of-domain-sample-identities`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** malformed-input-handling
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** The XM instrument loader imposes no 16-slot bound on declared sample count or note-map byte values, so a malformed XM can carry samples with sampleIndex >= 16 and map entries 16-255 into an editable copy where they are invisible in every presentation surface yet still present in the palette, and Export XM then fails for the whole document.

**Evidence:** PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:140 (`sampleCount = Int(readLE16(...))`, loop at 187-231 creates PlaybackSample with sampleIndex 0..<sampleCount unbounded by 16), PlaybackSongBuilder.swift readNoteSampleMap returns raw bytes 0-255 unclamped. Downstream: SampleSlotPresentationProjection.representedSamples filters indices to 0..<16 (PlaybackModel.swift:580-585) so slots >= 16 are hidden; selectedEmptySamplePopulationDestination/nextAppendSampleIndex/duplicate/permutation all reject (BlankTrackerDocument.swift:1088, 1123, 1422, 1272-1279); EditableXMWriter throws unsupportedSampleIndexOrder/unsupportedNoteSampleMap (EditableXMWriter.swift:302-310, 456-478), so the editable document becomes permanently un-exportable while remaining editable.

**Reachability:** synthetic/noncanonical only

**Invariant affected:** Canonical sample identity domain S01..S16 (zero-based 0..15) for every represented sample and map entry inside an editable document

**Why it matters:** A user who makes an editable copy of such a file can invest composition work into a document that can never pass Export XM (the only persistence route), hitting an error alert at save time instead of at copy time; hidden out-of-domain samples also make Equatable-based snapshots and displayed state disagree.

**Reproduction / proof:** Proposed: craft an XM declaring 17 sample headers (one with payload at index 16) or a note-map byte of 200; load; Make Editable Copy; observe the sample list shows nothing at slot 17 while instrumentPalette contains it; Export XM presents 'unsupported' failure.

**Existing mitigation:** Every canonical mutation defensively rejects out-of-domain state, so no further corruption occurs; export fails loudly rather than writing bad XM.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Clamp/reject at load or at the Make Editable Copy gate (LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator.unavailableReason) so out-of-domain sample identities either block the copy with the existing 'unsupported subset' message or are dropped/normalized before entering the editable model.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test: editable-copy gate rejects (or normalizes) a PlaybackSong containing sampleIndex 16 or map entry 16, and an accepted copy always round-trips through EditableXMWriter without throwing.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability synthetic/noncanonical only, confidence High): Confirmed with a significant route correction. The loader facts are accurate (unbounded sampleCount, unclamped note-map bytes) and all downstream mitigation/failure citations check out. However, the reporter's proposed repro via Make Editable Copy is WRONG: LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator.makeSupportedEditableCopy applies matchesLoadedSampleCopyBoundary (rejects represented sample indices and note-map entries outside 0..<16) AND a trial EditableXMWriter export at copy time, so that path fails loudly at copy time with 'This module cannot be converted into the current supported editable subset.' — the reporter's central harm claim ('error at save time instead of at copy time') does not hold for that route. The defect IS reachable via a different supported command: Clear Song Data on a loaded module (AppDelegate.clearSongData) is gated only by the weak loadedModuleCanMakeEditableCopy() check (any non-empty pcm) and calls BlankTrackerDocument.makeEditableCopyClearingSongData, which copies playbackSong.instrumentsByIndex wholesale with no sample-index bound, no note-map validation, and no trial export. Via that path a malformed XM (sampleIndex >= 16 with payload, or note-map byte 16-255) yields an editable document whose out-of-domain samples are invisible in every presentation surface (validSampleIndices filter), immune to every canonical mutation (all guards reject), and permanently un-exportable (EditableXMWriter throws). Recommended fix direction: route the Clear Song Data editable-copy gate through LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator's boundary check (or apply matchesLoadedSampleCopyBoundary + trial export inside makeEditableCopyClearingSongData), and/or clamp at the loader. Severity stays LOW: requires a deliberately crafted noncanonical XM (real FT2 writers cap at 16 samples/instrument), failure is loud at export, no silent XM corruption and no corruption of the source file; worst case is composition effort invested in an un-exportable document. Reachability stays synthetic/noncanonical only.

#### VTX-A1-004 — EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.replaceDocument never verifies that the live document still equals the closure-captured expectedCurrentDocument before overwriti

- **ID:** VTX-A1-004 (`A1-lifecycle-model:stale-snapshot-trap-no-expected-doc-check`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** robustness
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.replaceDocument never verifies that the live document still equals the closure-captured expectedCurrentDocument before overwriting it, and applyEdit performs no invariant validation on updatedDocument; correctness currently rests entirely on the convention that every non-coordinator blankDocument mutation either discards undo history or only changes selection/navigation.

**Evidence:** EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.swift:297-324 (replaceDocument guards only `contextProvider().documentAvailableForMutation != nil`; the `replacing expectedCurrentDocument:` parameter is used solely to register the reciprocal closure, never compared to the live document), EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.swift:66-75 (applyEdit accepts any BlankTrackerDocument value). Current conventions that keep it safe: AppDelegate.swift:1830-1882 (selection changes bypass coordinator, no discard), AppDelegate.swift:1259-1330 (order/pattern navigation bypasses, no discard), AppDelegate.swift:2484-2485 and 1510-1512 (all other direct mutations discard history).

**Reachability:** loaded/read-only only

**Invariant affected:** Undo must restore the exact pre-edit state without clobbering interleaved changes

**Why it matters:** The design is coherent today (undo intentionally restores selection/navigation, asserted by EditableDocumentEditCoordinatorTests.swift:343-345, 671-673), but the missing expected-current check is a latent trap: the first future code path that mutates blankDocument content directly without calling discardUndoHistory will make undo silently overwrite that change with a stale whole-document snapshot, with no assertion or log. This class of bug already forced the pattern-edit path to discard history entirely.

**Reproduction / proof:** Model-only demonstration: applyEdit(A->B); mutate context document to C outside the coordinator (as selectSampleSlot does for selection); coordinator.undo() applies snapshot A wholesale, discarding C's difference. Today C only ever differs in selection/navigation, so the result is accepted behavior.

**Existing mitigation:** MainActor confinement plus the discard-history convention at every content-mutating bypass; documentRevision staleness gates in the clear/move/swap/WAV coordinators prevent stale commits from that direction.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** In replaceDocument, compare contextProvider().documentAvailableForMutation against expectedCurrentDocument (ignoring or accepting selection drift explicitly) and bail out plus removeAllActions on mismatch, so a future convention violation fails safe instead of silently reverting user work.

**Recommended timing:** next milestone

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test: register an edit, mutate the harness context document out-of-band (non-selection field), call undo, assert the coordinator refuses/clears history rather than applying the stale snapshot.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability synthetic/noncanonical only, confidence High): Finding confirmed as described, with one reachability correction. All cited evidence checks out: replaceDocument guards only mutability, never compares the live document to expectedCurrentDocument (used only in the reciprocal registerUndo closure); applyEdit performs no invariant validation on updatedDocument; the documentApplyHandler (applyEditableDocumentSnapshot) also applies snapshots unconditionally. I independently enumerated all 13 blankDocument assignment sites (AppDelegate.swift is the sole assigner): every content-mutating bypass calls discardUndoHistory (lines 690, 1351, 1626, 1645, 1677, 1765, 2485) and the only non-discarding bypasses are selection/navigation-only (1267, 1305, 1838, 1867), so the convention holds everywhere today and no current workflow can trigger the clobber — hence severity stays LOW (latent trap, not a live defect). Refutation attempts failed: no hidden guard exists, no unprotected content bypass exists, and while a strict whole-document expected-current check would conflict with the intentional selection-restoring undo semantics (tests assert selection is deliberately restored on undo, EditableDocumentEditCoordinatorTests.swift:343-345, 671-673), a content-excluding-selection comparison or debug assertion remains feasible, so the gap is real. Mitigation claims verified: MainActor confinement; documentIdentity+documentRevision staleness gates in move/swap capture (SampleEditorSlotPermutationCapture.isCurrent) and WAV import coordinator. Reachability correction: reporter said 'loaded/read-only only', but the coordinator is inert for loaded modules (.loadedReadOnly context blocks all mutation); the demonstrated failure is model-only/future-code-path, so 'synthetic/noncanonical only' is the accurate classification. Not OBSERVATION: the missing defensive check with correctness resting on an unstated cross-file convention spanning 13 sites is genuine scheduled-cleanup-grade debt, evidenced by the pattern-edit path (2484-2485) opting out of undo integration entirely.

Test testWAVImportDoesNotMutateBeforeCandidateCompletesAndRejectsStaleAsyncResult (SampleEditorWindowControllerTests.swift:1837-1873) codifies the silent-finish behavior.

#### VTX-C1-002 — An XM that matches the 'Extended Module: ' magic but fails strict validation falls through to the MOD detector, which accepts any file >= 1084 bytes with four p

- **ID:** VTX-C1-002 (`C1-xm-parser:corrupt-xm-fallthrough-misdetected-as-mod`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** format-detection
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** An XM that matches the 'Extended Module: ' magic but fails strict validation falls through to the MOD detector, which accepts any file >= 1084 bytes with four printable bytes at offset 1080, reporting a MOD with garbage title instead of an invalid-XM error.

**Evidence:** core/ModuleCore/src/module_types.c:80-93 (XM attempt then MOD attempt, generic final error). core/ModuleCore/src/mod_header.c:19-27 (is_printable_sig), 73-89 (size>=1084 plus printable sig is sufficient; unknown sig only warns and defaults to 4 channels). Executed proof (edge_harness case1): 2048-byte buffer with valid XM header but packed_size beyond EOF -> xm_ok=0, mod_ok=1, type=MOD, title='Extended Module: EDG', warning='unknown MOD signature, defaulting to 4 channels'.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Malformed input is rejected with an accurate reason; module type reported to the user reflects actual detection confidence

**Why it matters:** Users opening a truncated or hostile XM >= 1084 bytes see it load as a 'MOD' with a mangled title (first 20 bytes of the XM signature) rather than a clear invalid-XM error; the MOD path then shows metadata-only UI and PlaybackSongBuilder rejects playback with an unrelated unsupported-type message.

**Reproduction / proof:** temporary /tmp harness `edge_harness.c` case1 (compiled against tracked sources, output captured); equivalently truncate any real XM's pattern data while keeping length >= 1084 and open it.

**Existing mitigation:** No unsafety: fuzzing showed no memory errors; MOD path is metadata-display-only and playback refuses non-XM.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** In mc_parse_file, if the buffer begins with 'Extended Module: ' but mc_parse_xm_header_bytes rejects it, return an XM-specific parse error instead of attempting MOD detection.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** ModuleCoreTests case: truncated-XM-with-1084+-bytes asserts ok=0 and error mentions XM, not MOD.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding confirmed exactly as reported, at the reporter's severity. I traced all three cited code sites and independently reproduced the fallthrough with my own temporary /tmp harness compiled from tracked sources (`refute_harness.c`): a 2048-byte buffer with a structurally valid XM header (magic, 0x1A at 37, header_size=20, 4ch/1pat) whose first pattern declares packed_size=0xFFFF beyond EOF yields xm_ok=0 then mod_ok=1 with type=MOD, title='Extended Module: EDG', warning='unknown MOD signature, defaulting to 4 channels'. Root cause: mc_parse_file has no notion of 'matched XM magic but failed validation' — it silently falls through to the MOD detector, whose acceptance criteria are only size>=1084 plus 4 printable bytes at offset 1080; an unrecognized signature merely warns and defaults to 4 channels. Reachable from File > Open (NSOpenPanel allows .data, i.e. any file) -> loadModule -> ModuleMetadataLoader.load -> mc_parse_file. Mitigating factors verified: PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:36-37 guards type=="XM" and throws unsupportedModuleType for the spurious MOD, so no playback; loaded modules are read-only so no state corruption; no memory unsafety in either parser path for this input. Caveat: for an organically truncated real XM the misdetection additionally requires the 4 bytes at offset 1080 to be printable (not guaranteed, but plausible; crafted files trigger it deterministically). Impact is limited to misleading type identification and mangled title/error UX for malformed input — LOW is correct, neither inflated nor deflated. Cheap fix if scheduled: have mc_parse_xm_header_bytes distinguish 'signature matched but invalid' from 'not XM' (e.g. tri-state return or sticky flag) and let mc_parse_file report an invalid-XM error instead of attempting MOD. coverage.readFully: core/ModuleCore/src/module_types.c, core/ModuleCore/src/mod_header.c, core/ModuleCore/src/xm_header.c, app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/ModuleMetadataLoader.swift.

#### VTX-C1-005 — One load performs three independent reads of the module file (C mc_parse_file, then two Data(contentsOf:) re-reads by the Swift walkers); the Swift walkers omit

- **ID:** VTX-C1-005 (`C1-xm-parser:swift-walkers-rely-on-c-gate-across-separate-file-reads`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** toctou-defense-in-depth
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** One load performs three independent reads of the module file (C mc_parse_file, then two Data(contentsOf:) re-reads by the Swift walkers); the Swift walkers omit the C gate's safety caps (notably no rowCount <= 256 clamp), so a file that changes between reads is walked with validation the gate never applied.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/ModuleMetadataLoader.swift:108 (mc_parse_file read 1), 391 (Data(contentsOf:) read 2), 415 (rowCount = max(1, readLE16) with no upper clamp vs xm_header.c:214 rejecting >256); PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:102 (read 3); AppDelegate.swift:1657-1690 (loadModule performs all three in sequence). Every individual byte access in both Swift walkers is bounds-checked (verified end-to-end: ModuleMetadataLoader.swift:387-525, PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:97-246), so this is allocation/consistency exposure, not memory unsafety.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** All structure walked in one load session was validated against the same bytes

**Why it matters:** If the file is replaced between reads (file being re-exported/downloaded while opened), parseXMPatternsFromFile can honor a crafted rowCount up to 65535 across up to 256 patterns and 64 channels (cell allocation in the multi-GB range -> memory exhaustion), or the app can end up with metadata, patterns, and instruments taken from different file versions.

**Reproduction / proof:** Proposed (race required): open a valid XM while atomically replacing it with one whose pattern headers declare rowCount 65535 between the C parse and the Swift re-read; alternatively unit-test parseXMPatternsFromFile directly with such bytes to show the missing clamp.

**Existing mitigation:** The C gate does run on every supported load and rejects rowCount 0/>256, channels >64, patterns >256 (proven by ModuleCoreTests:153-197 and edge harness); divergence requires a mid-load file mutation; all reads remain individually bounds-checked (760k ASan/UBSan fuzz iterations clean).

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Read the file into a single Data buffer once per load and hand the same bytes to the C bridge and both Swift walkers; additionally clamp rowCount to 1...256 in ModuleMetadataLoader.parseXMPatternsFromFile (one-line defense).

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test feeding parseXMPatternsFromFile bytes with rowCount 65535 asserts nil/clamped result; code review that loadModule performs exactly one file read.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Core claims confirmed by direct code trace: one load performs three independent file reads, and the Swift walkers omit the C gate's caps (notably no rowCount<=256 clamp at ModuleMetadataLoader.swift:415 vs xm_header.c:214 rejecting >MC_MAX_XM_PATTERN_ROWS=256). Both Swift walkers are individually bounds-checked (re-verified end-to-end), so this is consistency/allocation exposure only, and only under a mid-load file-replacement race. CORRECTION to the reporter's impact analysis: the "multi-GB cell allocation" scenario is overstated. (a) Array(repeating: innerRow, count: rowCount) at ModuleMetadataLoader.swift:423-426 CoW-shares one inner buffer across all rows, so up-front allocation is ~8 bytes/row (~134 MB for 256 patterns x 65535 rows with packedSize=0, not multi-GB). (b) Per-row materialization is bounded by packedSize (UInt16 <= 65535 bytes, >=1 byte/event via the offset<length guard at line 467); overflow makes decodeXMPatternEvent return nil, parseXMPatternsFromFile returns nil, and parseXMPatterns falls back at line 315 to parseXMPatternsFromInfo, which uses the C-gate-validated pattern_row_counts. Also, channel count comes from the C parse of the ORIGINAL file (clamped <=64 at xm_header.c:151), so the attacker-swapped file cannot raise it. Realistic worst case is order 10^2 MB transient plus version-skewed metadata/patterns/instruments and rowCount>256 patterns reaching the UI model — degradation and inconsistency, not exhaustion or unsafety. Reachability: loadModule (open module) is a supported workflow, but divergence additionally requires an external process to atomically replace the file between reads; no in-app path triggers it. LOW severity and defense-in-depth categorization are appropriate; a cheap fix is clamping rowCount to 256 in parseXMPatternsFromFile (or reusing info.pattern_row_counts), or reading the file bytes once and sharing them across all three consumers.

#### VTX-C2-003 — For loopType 0 the writer emits loopStartBytes=0/loopLengthBytes=0, but PlaybackSongBuilder preserves a nonzero loopStart for disabled-loop samples at load, so

- **ID:** VTX-C2-003 (`C2-xm-writer-copy:disabled-loop-start-dropped-on-export`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** round-trip-fidelity
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** For loopType 0 the writer emits loopStartBytes=0/loopLengthBytes=0, but PlaybackSongBuilder preserves a nonzero loopStart for disabled-loop samples at load, so a foreign XM with disabled-loop-but-stored loop points loses them through Make Editable Copy -> Export (FT2 users who re-enable the loop later find their loop start reset to 0).

**Why it matters:** Wild FT2 files commonly retain loop start/length values in headers with the loop type bits cleared; after copy+export the reopened PlaybackSample.loopStart differs from the in-memory value (n -> 0), silently breaking value-preservation for that field and discarding user data relevant to other trackers, though VTX playback semantics are identical (loop off either way).

**Reproduction / proof:** Write a small XM whose sample header has type=0, loopStart=100, loopLength=50; load -> loaded sample.loopStart==clamped 100; make editable copy -> export -> reopen: loopStart==0.

**Existing mitigation:** VTX-canonical documents always carry loopStart 0 with loopType 0 (import sets 0; VTX exports write 0), so VTX-only round trips are unaffected; the reader already drops loopLength for type 0, limiting what could be preserved anyway.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Emit the clamped stored loopStart (and loopLength) bytes even when loopType==0, mirroring the reader's preservation, or document the field as intentionally normalized in docs/format-changes.md.

**Recommended timing:** post-v1

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Round-trip test: type-0 sample with nonzero loop fields survives load -> copy -> export -> reopen with loopStart preserved (or a doc note declaring normalization).

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Traced end-to-end: foreign XM with type=0 and nonzero stored loopStart -> loader preserves clamped loopStart in PlaybackSample (loopLength already zeroed at parse) -> makeEditableCopy adopts playbackSong.instrumentsByIndex as instrumentPalette with no loop normalization, and isCompleteRepresentedSample explicitly admits loopType==0 with any loopStart>=0 -> EditableXMWriter.exportedSample writes loopStartBytes=0/loopLengthBytes=0 for loopType==0 -> reopen yields loopStart 0. Corrections to reporter's framing: (1) loop LENGTH for disabled loops is already discarded at load (safeLoopLengthInSamples returns 0 for type 0), so a writer-only fix cannot restore full dormant-loop fidelity; (2) in-memory loopStart is clamped to sample length at load, so byte-exact preservation is impossible in out-of-range edge cases regardless. VTX playback is identical either way (loop off), VTX-canonical imports set loopStart 0 (WAVSampleImportDecoder.swift:184), so only foreign-XM -> Make Editable Copy -> Export round trips are affected, and only if the user later re-enables the loop in another tracker. LOW severity and supported-workflow reachability as reported are both accurate; no inflation or deflation needed.

Repro checks out: ch0=D05 + ch1=D10 -> VTX breaks to row 5, FT2 to row 10. I also found a related divergence the reporter missed, same root cause: FT2's positionJump resets pBreakPos to 0, so Dxx on a lower channel + Bxx on a higher channel yields row 0 in FT2, but VTX's combined-Bxx+Dxx policy (bxx_uses_dxx_row_target_when_same_row) always applies the Dxx row regardless of channel order. Severity LOW is correct: deterministic wrong-path only when a row carries conflicting jump commands on multiple channels (rare in real modules), no crash/corruption; single-command rows match FT2. Fix direction if scheduled: resolve Bxx/Dxx per-row by emulating FT2's last-writer-wins overwrite semantics including positionJump's pBreakPos reset.

Mechanism: the chunk loop's data branch reads the whole chunk via read_exact when fmt is None, and read_data_chunk (the only place `seconds` is honored, line 244) is bypassed; stats_for then derives frames_analyzed/duration_analyzed from the full decoded list while requested_seconds is echoed verbatim (line 992). One correction to the reporter's invariant claim: pairwise diff/correlation metrics truncate to min(len(reference), len(candidate)) (diff_metrics line 795, normalized_correlation line 339), so with one conforming file the cross-file diffs still cover only the requested window (overlap_frames=4000 in repro); only per-file stats and analyzed-duration deltas mislead unless BOTH files are data-first. Reachability: data-before-fmt violates RIFF/WAVE chunk ordering; documented inputs (openmpt123/mikmod/VTX renders) are fmt-first, so this needs a hand-crafted nonconforming WAV. LOW (not OBSERVATION) because the divergence is silent in a tool whose report claims to describe the analyzed window; not higher because it is a diagnostic script edge case with no product-code or data-integrity impact.

No guard exists: the except (AnalysisError, wave.Error, OSError) at line 833 never fires because nothing raises. Correction to secondary claim: the per-channel RMS denominator at lines 239-242 does use info.frame_count while overall RMS (line 243) uses sample_count, but the discrepancy is unreachable as a standalone defect — the loop only terminates when frame_index == info.frame_count, so frames decoded always equals the header count whenever line 239 executes. It is a latent bug that becomes live only when the hang is fixed with an early exit on empty read, and must be co-fixed then. Severity LOW is correct (developer diagnostic tooling; docs/diagnostic-tools.md:61 lists it as local-only/candidate-archive; not app runtime or user-data path). tools/audio_compare_tests.py (DISCONTINUITY_SCRIPT_PATH, line 16) exercises the script in tests but only with well-formed WAVs, which is why the hang was never caught; the script is otherwise manually invoked per docs/reports/audio-comparison-history.md. Fix shape: break out of the while loop when chunk_frames == 0 (raise AnalysisError for truncation, or warn) and compute per-channel RMS over frames actually decoded.

#### VTX-CS-024 — parse_byte in the coverage summarizer interprets any string of length <= 2 as hexadecimal, so a decimal string like "12" becomes 0x12 (18), silently mislabeling

- **ID:** VTX-CS-024 (`CS-effect-scan-scripts:parse-byte-decimal-string-hex-ambiguity`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** correctness-robustness
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** parse_byte in the coverage summarizer interprets any string of length <= 2 as hexadecimal, so a decimal string like "12" becomes 0x12 (18), silently mislabeling effect types/params if a diagnostics producer ever serializes bytes as decimal strings.

**Evidence:** scripts/summarize-xm-effect-coverage.py lines 255-274: 'if len(text) <= 2 or any(ch in "abcdefABCDEF" for ch in text): return int(text, 16) & 0xFF' runs before the base-10 branch, so all 1-2 character digit strings are parsed as hex; only 3+ character pure-digit strings get base 10.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Effect command labeling (effect_command_label lines 391-447) must map the actual byte values; a 0x12 vs 12 confusion changes the command row entirely (e.g. '2xx portamento down' vs 'Ixx unknown/unsupported').

**Why it matters:** The heuristic is undocumented and produces silent misclassification instead of an error for ambiguous inputs; current in-repo producers emit JSON integers so it is latent, but the tool also accepts hand-fed traces.

**Reproduction / proof:** python3 -c on /tmp: import the script module; parse_byte("12") returns 18, parse_byte("112") returns 112 — inconsistent radix for the same notation.

**Existing mitigation:** In-repo diagnostics and runtime traces serialize these fields as JSON numbers, which take the int/float branches (lines 258-261) and are handled correctly.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Restrict string parsing to explicit 0x-prefixed hex plus base-10 otherwise (or require integers and error on strings), and document the accepted formats in the module docstring.

**Recommended timing:** post-v1

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test parse_byte over decimal strings, 0x-prefixed strings, and bare hex; assert one documented radix policy.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability synthetic/noncanonical only, confidence High): The code-level claim is real and reproduced: parse_byte treats any 1-2 char string as hex before trying base 10, so parse_byte("12")=18 while parse_byte("112")=112 (inconsistent radix), and effect_command_label("12","0") yields "Ixx unknown/unsupported" while effect_command_label(12,0) yields "Cxx set volume". However, two corrections to the reporter: (1) reachability is NOT a supported user workflow — the offline diagnostics producer emits JSON integers (BoundedXMRenderTool.swift, Int(...) at lines 1218/1240/1515 etc.) which hit the correct int branch, and the runtime trace producer emits zero-padded 2-char unprefixed hex strings via hexByte (RuntimeCMixerDiagnostics.swift:1440-1442, String(format:"%02X")), for which the len<=2 hex branch is the CORRECT and deliberately load-bearing interpretation; no in-repo producer can trigger the misparse, only hand-authored decimal-string traces. (2) The reporter's mitigation statement ("runtime traces serialize these fields as JSON numbers") is wrong — they are hex strings, which is precisely why the heuristic exists and why real traces parse correctly. Residual issue is localized robustness/clarity: the heuristic is uncommented and silently returns a wrong byte for ambiguous hand-fed decimal strings instead of erroring. LOW is the severity ceiling; OBSERVATION would also be defensible. No change to any supported pipeline output.

#### VTX-CS-025 — The residual scanner classifies effects against channel state from before the same row's note is applied and never clears active_voice on key-off/note-cut, so K

- **ID:** VTX-CS-025 (`CS-effect-scan-scripts:scan-state-model-preapply-misclassification`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** correctness-heuristic
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** The residual scanner classifies effects against channel state from before the same row's note is applied and never clears active_voice on key-off/note-cut, so Kxx/Rxy/A00/3xx/5xy occurrences on note-trigger rows are counted as no_active and rows after key-off are counted as active.

**Evidence:** scripts/summarize-xm-residual-effect-scan.py: scan_module lines 420-428 calls scan_effect_cell before apply_note_state; apply_note_state lines 689-698 has 'elif cell.note == 97: state.active_voice = state.active_voice' (self-assignment no-op, key-off never deactivates); scan_kxx lines 650-665, scan_rxy lines 630-647, scan_axy lines 555-573, scan_3xx lines 530-552 all branch on state.active_voice. Also Fxx speed is applied to the next row only (lines 426-429 set next_speed; speed = next_speed after the row) whereas FT2 applies Fxx from the current row, affecting out_of_row_no_op classification for Kxx/Rxy on the same row; Bxx/Dxx/E6x order-flow is ignored so rows never actually played are still scanned.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Diagnostic classification counts (applied/no_active/out_of_row) should approximate actual playback semantics closely enough to guide prioritization.

**Why it matters:** no_active and out-of-row counts are systematically biased for rows that both trigger a note and carry an effect, and after key-off rows; since the reports drive freeze-exit evidence, the bias could mildly distort which residuals look real. Purely diagnostic; no playback impact.

**Reproduction / proof:** Under /tmp harness: ModuleData with row [Cell(note=48, instrument=1, effect_type=0x14, effect_param=0x01)] at speed 6 classifies Kxx as no_active_count although the note triggers a voice on the same row's tick 0 before tick 1 key-off.

**Existing mitigation:** The scripts are explicitly diagnostics-only, the top-level recommendation is a frozen constant, and coordinates let a human inspect first occurrences manually.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Apply the same-row note trigger to ChannelState before effect classification (or classify with post-note state for tick>=1 effects), model note 97/Kxx/ECx as deactivating, and apply Fxx speed to the current row; alternatively document the known biases in the script docstring.

**Recommended timing:** post-v1

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Add tools/xm_residual_effect_scan_tests.py cases: note+Kxx same row asserts applied_count; row after note 97 asserts no_active for Axy; Fxx speed change row asserts out_of_row classification uses the new speed.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability build/CI only, confidence High): CONFIRMED with two corrections. (1) Reachability: this is a maintainer-run, local-only diagnostic script over a private corpus label map (docs/diagnostic-tools.md:65), never executed in the shipped app or any supported user workflow — the reporter's "supported user workflow" is an overstatement; closest schema category is build/CI-style developer tooling. (2) The key-off half of the claim is weaker than stated: keeping active_voice true after note 97 is a defensible heuristic (enveloped voices keep sounding through release; even non-envelope FT2 channels keep processing effects), though the self-assignment at 697-698 is literal dead code and the available envelope info is unused. The core bias is real and material for the tables it feeds: effects on note-trigger rows are classified against pre-note channel state, so Kxx/Rxy/5xy/3xx/A00 co-located with a note (the common authoring pattern for Kxx) are systematically miscounted as no_active, and same-row Fxx speed changes are applied one row late, skewing out_of_row classifications. Impact is bounded: recommend_next_pr is a frozen freeze constant independent of counts, coordinates allow manual inspection, and no playback code is involved. Severity LOW is correct (not OBSERVATION, because the misclassification is systematic on a common pattern and the counts are cited as freeze-exit evidence; not MEDIUM, because it is diagnostics-only with a count-independent recommendation).
