#### VTX-D1-003 — Volume/pan envelope loop wrapping is gated on key_on, so after key-off a looped envelope stops looping and clamps at its final point during fadeout, diverging f

- **ID:** VTX-D1-003 (`D1-runtime-cmixer:envelope-loop-stops-after-keyoff`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** Medium
- **Category:** xm-parity
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** Volume/pan envelope loop wrapping is gated on key_on, so after key-off a looped envelope stops looping and clamps at its final point during fadeout, diverging from FT2 behavior where envelope loops continue after key-off.

**Evidence:** vtx_c_mixer.c:402-422 vtx_c_mixer_advance_envelope: sustain hold correctly requires key_on (405-411), but the loop wrap at 415-421 also requires key_on. Instrument envelopes are wired into this path via the adapter (PlaybackSongAdapter+RuntimeEvents.swift:700-796 maps instrument volume envelopes to MixerEnvelope; RuntimeCMixerRenderCore.swift:1566-1577 passes event.volumeEnvelope into addVoice).

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** XM instrument envelope semantics: envelope loop continues to cycle after key-off; only the sustain point is released.

**Why it matters:** Modules using looped volume envelopes (pulsing/tremolo-style instruments) sound wrong after key-off: the pulse freezes at the last envelope value while the fadeout runs, in both runtime playback and offline export.

**Reproduction / proof:** Load an XM whose instrument has a looped volume envelope (no sustain) and a long fadeout; play a note followed by key-off (note 97). Expected (FT2/ft2-clone): amplitude keeps cycling during fadeout. Actual: amplitude freezes at the envelope's final point value.

**Existing mitigation:** Only audible on instruments combining envelope loops with key-off fades; sustain-based envelopes behave correctly.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Drop the key_on condition from the loop-wrap branch (keep it on the sustain hold), matching FT2 envelope processing.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** C-core unit test: looped envelope voice with key_off_frame set; assert envelope position wraps after key-off. Cross-check one reference module against ft2-clone rendering.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding is real exactly as described. vtx_c_mixer_advance_envelope gates the envelope loop wrap on key_on, so after key-off (note 97) a looped volume/pan envelope stops cycling and clamps at its final point value while fadeout runs. FT2 reference (ft2-clone ft2_replayer.c:1501-1516) wraps the loop after key-off unless sustain is enabled AND the sustain point equals the loop end; VTX suppresses all post-key-off wrapping. Full path is reachable in supported playback: note-97 key-off events are planned (PlaybackSongAdapter.swift:244, 932-945), keyOffFrame is passed to addVoice (RuntimeCMixerRenderCore.swift:1561-1577), and the C render loop flips key_on at the scheduled frame (vtx_c_mixer.c:1949, 462-469) then advances envelopes per frame (1976). The Lxx envelope-position mechanism is effect-triggered only and does not override this. Correction to reporter framing: this is a documented first-pass approximation, not a silent bug — docs/design/parsed-xm-to-c-mixer-adapter.md:163-166, 508, 688-690 explicitly scope loop wrapping to 'while keyed-on', and docs/decisions/003-first-pass-playback-accuracy.md:105-109 disclaims exact FT2 envelope parity. LOW severity is appropriate: audible fidelity divergence only, niche instrument configuration (looped envelope + key-off + nonzero fadeout), no state corruption, no effect on exported XM data. Worth scheduling as an XM-parity item since post-key-off loop continuation is core envelope semantics, not an edge quirk.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** UI test: audition a short one-shot fixture, wait past its duration, assert the audition indicator returns to off (or that one click restarts audition).

The Sample Editor audition button state is derived solely from activeAuditionToken; the audio sink stack (EditorNoteAuditionPreviewCommandHandoff -> EditorNoteAuditionCoreAudioOutputHost -> EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink) exposes no voice-completion callback and nothing polls handoff diagnostics (lastRenderedGeneration/outstandingVoiceCount). The only sink-to-UI notification is previewInvalidationHandler, fired only on output route/format change. The C mixer's no-loop policy deactivates the voice when sample data exhausts (CSoftwareMixer.swift:310), so for non-looping samples audio ends while the button still shows the stop glyph and red LED; the next click is a release no-op and a second click is required to re-audition. All mitigation paths the reporter listed were verified (selection/source change, window resign, window close, document transition). Severity LOW is correct: cosmetic UI/audio state divergence on a supported alpha surface, self-correcting, no data or corruption risk. Design nuance: the token models an audition gate (needed for looping samples), so a fix would be a completion signal or poll rather than a redesign of the toggle.

#### VTX-D2-004 — When Play arrives while an adapter-plan prewarm is still running, the main thread blocks on an NSCondition waiting for work executing on a .utility-QoS dispatch

- **ID:** VTX-D2-004 (`D2-preview-transport:prewarm-wait-qos-inversion`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** performance
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** When Play arrives while an adapter-plan prewarm is still running, the main thread blocks on an NSCondition waiting for work executing on a .utility-QoS dispatch queue; NSCondition provides no priority donation, so under CPU contention the main-thread stall can exceed what the synchronous fallback (which runs at the caller's QoS) would take.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/PlaybackEngine.swift: DispatchQueueRuntimeAdapterPlanPrewarmScheduler queue qos .utility lines 114-118; DispatchQueueRuntimeAdapterPlanPrewarmJob.waitForResult condition wait lines 89-97; waitForRuntimeAdapterPlanPrewarmIfNeeded called from prepareRuntimeAdapterEventPlanIfNeeded on @MainActor lines 977 and 1072-1107 (job.waitForResult() at line 1080).

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Transport start should not stall the main thread longer than necessary

**Why it matters:** Pressing Play immediately after loading a large module (before prewarm completes) blocks the UI for the remaining plan-make time, amplified by QoS inversion under load; it degrades perceived transport latency but corrupts nothing.

**Reproduction / proof:** Load a long multi-pattern module and press Play immediately (within the prewarm window) while the machine is CPU-loaded; compare the runtime_adapter_event_plan_prewarm_wait phase in the timing trace against runtime_adapter_event_plan_make in sync-fallback mode.

**Existing mitigation:** Prewarm usually completes before the user hits Play; plan make is bounded by song size; timing traces already record the wait phase for diagnosis.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Raise the prewarm queue QoS to .userInitiated, or wait via a QoS-propagating primitive, or cancel-and-run-synchronously when Play must wait.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Timing-trace comparison of prewarm_wait durations under synthetic CPU load before/after the QoS change.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Traced the full chain and could not refute. Production default scheduler is DispatchQueueRuntimeAdapterPlanPrewarmScheduler (PlaybackEngine.init default param, line 241) whose serial queue is created with explicit qos: .utility (115-118). @MainActor PlaybackEngine (160): play() line 469 and seek-with-autoplay line 563 call prepareRuntimeAdapterEventPlanIfNeeded; when the cached plan is not yet generated and a matching prewarm job is pending (scheduled at load, lines 268-300 -> 780-812), line 977 -> waitForRuntimeAdapterPlanPrewarmIfNeeded -> job.waitForResult() (1080) -> NSCondition.wait loop (89-97) blocks the main thread. Technical QoS claim is accurate: a queue with an explicitly assigned QoS runs blocks at that QoS regardless of submitter propagation, and NSCondition (condition variable, no ownership) participates in no priority-donation mechanism, unlike DispatchWorkItem.wait/dispatch sync/os_unfair_lock. Refutation attempts failed: no deadlock (job.finish broadcasts directly on the utility queue at line 153 before the @MainActor completion Task, so wakeup does not depend on the main actor); no cancel-then-sync-fallback guard on the play path (sync fallback at 1017-1069 is only reached when no matching job exists or the job yields no plan); the scheduler's other consumer (requestEditablePatternLoopRefresh, 312-352) completes async and never blocks. Severity LOW is correct: wait is bounded by plan-make time; on an unloaded machine waiting on a mostly-done prewarm typically beats a fresh sync make; the degradation only manifests under CPU contention within the load-to-Play window; perceived-latency-only, nothing corrupts; the prewarm_wait timing phase (1089-1093) makes it diagnosable. Cheap remediations: DispatchWorkItem.wait (QoS override) or a higher/unspecified queue QoS. Does not block alpha.

#### VTX-D2-005 — The runtime C-mixer song-end stop timer is created with Timer.scheduledTimer (default run-loop mode only), unlike the tick and follow timers which are added for

- **ID:** VTX-D2-005 (`D2-preview-transport:song-end-stop-timer-runloop-mode`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** transport-lifecycle
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** The runtime C-mixer song-end stop timer is created with Timer.scheduledTimer (default run-loop mode only), unlike the tick and follow timers which are added for .common mode, so if a menu or event-tracking loop is active when the song-end tail elapses, the transport stays in 'playing' state after audio has already ended until tracking finishes.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/PlaybackEngine.swift lines 1230-1236 (Timer.scheduledTimer for runtimeCMixerSongEndStopTimer) versus lines 1156-1162 and 1264-1270 (Timer(timeInterval:) + RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common) for the tick timer and follow timer).

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Transport state should transition to stopped promptly at planned song end

**Why it matters:** A user holding a menu open across the song-end boundary sees the transport stuck in playing state (and isPlaying-gated controls stay disabled) even though mixer output ended; inconsistent with the deliberate .common-mode choice of the sibling timers.

**Reproduction / proof:** Play a short module to within a few seconds of its planned end, open and hold the application menu across the end + tail + 0.5s grace boundary; the stop (state change, playbackDidStop callback, control-panel resync) does not fire until the menu closes.

**Existing mitigation:** Pure UI-state delay: the c-mixer plan has already stopped producing events and the audible tail has elapsed; closing the menu fires the timer immediately.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Create the song-end stop timer the same way as the others (Timer(timeInterval:) + RunLoop.main.add(_, forMode: .common)).

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Existing runtime song-end tests plus a manual check with a held menu; or assert the timer's run-loop registration mode via a test seam.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Traced and confirmed exactly as reported. runtimeCMixerSongEndStopTimer is created via Timer.scheduledTimer (default run-loop mode only) while the sibling tick and follow timers are explicitly added to RunLoop.main for .common mode, showing the .common choice was deliberate elsewhere. Attempted refutations all failed: (1) the tick timer cannot serve as fallback because advanceOneTick's .ended branch calls holdTransportForRuntimeCMixerSongEndTailIfNeeded(), which invalidates the tick timer whenever runtimeCMixerSongEndStopPending is set (it is set at every plan-backed play start via scheduleRuntimeCMixerSongEndStopIfNeeded at lines 532/585), so it never reaches stop(reason:"planned_song_end") in the tail-hold case; (2) the .common-mode follow timer only publishes positions, never stops; (3) RuntimeCMixerBackend has no backend-to-engine song-end/stop callback — all stop references there are engine-to-backend; (4) the c-mixer path is the only runtime backend (AudioBackendSelection.resolve defaults to .cMixer and usesRuntimeCMixer is unconditionally true), so this is the standard playback path, not an opt-in mode. PlaybackEngine is @MainActor, so scheduledTimer lands on the main run loop as the reporter assumed. During NSMenu/event-tracking run-loop modes the .default-mode timer is deferred until tracking ends, leaving transport state .playing (and playbackDidStop/control resync deferred) after mixer output has ended. Impact is a self-healing UI-state delay only — the expired one-shot fires immediately when the run loop returns to default mode — with no state corruption, so LOW severity and supported-user-workflow reachability are both correct, neither inflated nor deflated. Fix is trivial: construct with Timer(timeInterval:repeats:block:) and add to RunLoop.main for .common like the siblings.

#### VTX-E-002 — PlaybackSongSyntheticAdapter.mixerSampleBuffer keys a cache on the raw storage address+count of sample.pcm but stores a mapped copy that does not retain the key

- **ID:** VTX-E-002 (`E-memory-safety:address-keyed-cache-without-storage-retention`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** aliasing-hazard
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** PlaybackSongSyntheticAdapter.mixerSampleBuffer keys a cache on the raw storage address+count of sample.pcm but stores a mapped copy that does not retain the keyed storage, so cache correctness depends on the un-documented invariant that all keyed pcm arrays stay alive for the cache's scope; address reuse (ABA) would serve the wrong sample's PCM.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/PlaybackSongAdapter+VolumeEffects.swift lines 6-22 (key from withUnsafeBufferPointer address; value MixerSampleBuffer); SoftwareMixer.swift lines 170-172 (MixerSampleBuffer.init maps to a NEW array, sharing nothing with the key's storage); cache scope PlaybackSongAdapter.swift line 383 (Context.mixerSampleBuffers, one adapt pass); keyed arrays are owned by the live PlaybackSong for that pass (PlaybackModel.swift lines 28-89: PlaybackSample derivatives share pcm storage). Contrast the deliberately-safe variant: CSoftwareMixerSharedSamplePayloadCache retains pcm exactly to pin the address key (CSoftwareMixer.swift lines 153-189, comment line 154).

**Reachability:** loaded/read-only only

**Invariant affected:** A cache keyed by storage address must pin that storage (or be provably scoped under owners that do) so a freed buffer's address cannot be reused by a different key-equal buffer.

**Why it matters:** Today every keyed array is retained by the song for the duration of the single-threaded adapt pass, so no live aliasing exists; but any future path that passes a temporarily-derived pcm array (e.g., sliced or processed PCM) can free it mid-pass and a same-length reallocation at the same address would return the wrong cached PCM — a silent wrong-audio bug that is very hard to diagnose.

**Reproduction / proof:** Proposed (requires code change): inside one adapt pass, feed mixerSampleBuffer two successive temporary [Float] arrays of identical length created/dropped in a loop; on allocator address reuse the second call returns the first array's cached buffer.

**Existing mitigation:** Cache is scoped to one adapt call; all current PlaybackSample.pcm arrays are owned by the live song; single-threaded use.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Retain the keyed array in the cache entry (matching CSoftwareMixerSharedSamplePayloadCache), or document the pinning invariant at the cache and assert it by construction (accept only song-owned samples).

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test that mutating/dropping a source array after caching cannot change lookup results; code comment/assert documenting the pinning rule.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability loaded/read-only only, confidence High): Finding confirmed exactly as described, including its own mitigations. The cache keys on raw pcm storage address+count and stores a value (MixerSampleBuffer, built via monoPCM.map which always allocates a new array) that does not retain the keyed storage. However, I traced the ONLY call site and every sample reaching it comes unmodified (CoW-shared) from song.instrumentsByIndex via selectSample/PlaybackInstrumentSampleResolver; no path constructs a temporary pcm array, and `song` is a live parameter for the whole adapt call, so every keyed buffer is retained for the cache's full scope — ABA address reuse is impossible in current code and the reporter's proposed repro correctly requires a code change. I also checked the empty-array storage-singleton collision case for refutation: unreachable, because isPlayable (PlaybackModel.swift:205-207) requires non-empty pcm before line 1735. The contrast with the deliberately-pinning CSoftwareMixerSharedSamplePayloadCache is real (comment at CSoftwareMixer.swift:157 explicitly retains pcm to pin the key identity). Severity LOW is the ceiling — this borders OBSERVATION since no demonstrated defect exists on any current input; I accept LOW as robustness debt because the hardening fix is one line (retain sample.pcm with the cached value, mirroring the C cache) and a future violation would manifest as silent wrong audio. Does not block alpha; reasonable to fold into any future touch of the adapter cache.

#### VTX-E-003 — The runtime note-trigger path uses CSoftwareMixer.addVoice, which routes every non-OK C status (including VTX_C_MIXER_STATUS_VOICE_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED) through re

- **ID:** VTX-E-003 (`E-memory-safety:addvoice-precondition-crash-on-voice-capacity`)
- **Severity:** LOW (reporter said MEDIUM; adversarial verification calibrated to LOW)
- **Confidence:** Medium
- **Category:** error-handling
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 2 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** The runtime note-trigger path uses CSoftwareMixer.addVoice, which routes every non-OK C status (including VTX_C_MIXER_STATUS_VOICE_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED) through requireOK, turning fixed-pool exhaustion into a release-build precondition crash instead of a dropped note.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/CSoftwareMixer.swift: addVoice lines 397-450 calls Self.requireOK(status) at line 433; requireOK lines 1119-1121 preconditions on any non-OK status. Runtime call sites: RuntimeCMixerRenderCore.swift lines 1445 (triggerWithDiagnostics) and 1566 (triggerAdapterEventWithDiagnosticsLocked). Contrast: addScheduledVoiceWithResult lines 488-573 returns typed CSoftwareMixerScheduledVoiceResult rejections for the same C statuses. Loaded slots persist for inactive voices until the same channel tag is retriggered or stopped (vtx_c_mixer.c: ramp completion sets active=0 but slot stays loaded, lines 436-447; release only in stop/rampDown/clear, lines 1188-1256, 1120-1133).

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** The realtime audio control path degrades gracefully under resource exhaustion; user input never crashes the app.

**Why it matters:** Voice-pool exhaustion (256 slots) during live triggering would abort the process. Normal workflows stay far below capacity (loaded count tracks channel count plus transient 32-frame ramps), so a crash is unlikely today, but the crash-vs-reject asymmetry between addVoice and addScheduledVoiceWithResult is a latent stability risk on the hot user-facing path.

**Reproduction / proof:** Proposed (code-change test, not runnable in workflows today): call mixer.addVoice 257 times with distinct channel tags on one CSoftwareMixer; the 257th call hits VTX_C_MIXER_STATUS_VOICE_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED and requireOK traps. In-app this requires >256 concurrently loaded slots, i.e., >256 distinct channel tags with lingering voices.

**Existing mitigation:** rampDownReplacementChannelLocked releases prior inactive voices per channel before each add; channel tags are bounded by module channel count (<=64); audition uses a separate single-voice mixer; offline paths already use the typed-result variant.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Add an addVoiceWithResult variant (or make addVoice return an optional index) and have the two runtime trigger sites treat capacity exhaustion as a diagnosed dropped note, reserving preconditions for genuine programmer errors.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test: fill the pool to 256 loaded voices, trigger one more via the runtime path, assert a typed rejection and no crash; assert diagnostics record the drop.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): The mechanical claim is fully accurate: runtime note triggers (RuntimeCMixerRenderCore.triggerWithDiagnostics line 1445 and triggerAdapterEventWithDiagnosticsLocked line 1566) call CSoftwareMixer.addVoice, which routes every non-OK C status through requireOK's precondition (trap in release), including VTX_C_MIXER_STATUS_VOICE_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, while addScheduledVoiceWithResult returns typed rejections for the identical statuses. I additionally verified an unreported second trap on the same path: malloc failure during sample copy (vtx_c_mixer.c lines 901-903) returns INVALID_ARGUMENT and also hits requireOK. However, I downgrade severity MEDIUM->LOW: the failure condition is not reachable from any supported workflow. rampDownReplacementChannelLocked (RuntimeCMixerRenderCore.swift 3618-3638) releases prior inactive loaded voices per channel tag before every add (vtx_c_mixer_ramp_down_voices_for_channel_tag lines 1239-1241 releases inactive slots); channel tags are bounded by module channel count (editable XM capped at 32, EditableXMWriter.swift lines 95/181); steady-state loaded slots are ~2 per channel and a pile-up requires retriggers within a 32-frame (~0.7ms) ramp window, impossible at tracker tick rates (>=~9.8ms at BPM 255). Audition uses a fully isolated single-voice mixer that clears before each add (EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink.swift lines 126, 146-147). So this is a localized crash-vs-reject asymmetry / latent robustness debt on the hot path, fixable by switching the two runtime call sites to a typed-result add and dropping the note on rejection; it does not represent a currently-triggerable crash. The reachability tag applies to the code path (it runs on every supported note trigger); the trapping condition itself is synthetic today. Minor secondary note: requireOK's message ("C mixer returned invalid argument") is misleading for capacity-exceeded.
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding is real exactly as described. addVoice converts recoverable C statuses (voice capacity at 256, malloc failure reported as INVALID_ARGUMENT) into a process-killing Swift precondition, and this call site executes inside the AURenderCallback-driven render chain of the default c_mixer backend (default per AudioBackendSelection.swift:47), so a trap would occur on the audio IO thread of the standard playback workflow. The scheduled-voice API (addScheduledVoiceWithResult) handles the identical statuses gracefully, proving graceful degradation was the intended pattern. Severity LOW is correct: the trap requires resource exhaustion that supported workflows do not reach — per-channel voice cleanup (rampDownReplacementChannelLocked before every add; vtx_c_mixer_ramp_down_voices_for_channel_tag releases stale inactive voices) bounds occupancy far below 256 for XM's max 32 channels, and macOS overcommit makes per-trigger sample-copy malloc failure rare. One correction to the reporter's mitigation text: naturally-finished voices are only deactivated during render (voice->active=0 at vtx_c_mixer.c:1951/1956), never released there; their slots stay loaded until the next same-channel trigger releases them — occupancy is still bounded, so the conclusion stands. Minor cosmetic issue: the precondition message says "invalid argument" even for capacity-exceeded. The proposed 257-add repro is sound. Fix direction (map addVoice statuses to a result like the scheduled API) is small and does not touch protected boundaries.

**Independently rediscovered by:** `D1-runtime-cmixer:addvoice-precondition-crash-on-capacity` (LOW) — merged into this finding; concurrence across independent auditors raises confidence.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/RuntimeCMixerOutputRouteDiagnostics.swift lines 133-150: value?.takeUnretainedValue() with no corresponding release; called via deviceUIDHash(for:) line 127-131 from currentDefaultOutputDevice() line 48. **Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Core Foundation Create/Copy-rule ownership: caller releases CF objects it receives ownership of.

**Why it matters:** Slow leak of small CFString allocations on every default-output-device or sample-rate change and every audio-graph diagnostics snapshot; harmless short-term but a real ownership bug and noise in leak tooling.

**Reproduction / proof:** Run the app under Instruments Leaks, toggle the system default output device several times (fires defaultOutputDidChange -> currentDefaultOutputDevice -> deviceUIDHash); each toggle leaks CFString instances attributed to stringProperty.

**Existing mitigation:** Query frequency is low (route changes, diagnostics snapshots); strings are tiny.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Change to value?.takeRetainedValue() (one line), matching CF ownership for AudioObjectGetPropertyData CFString results.

**Recommended timing:** next milestone

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Instruments Leaks run over repeated device toggles shows no CFString leak from stringProperty.

**Adversarial verification notes:**

All five cited call sites verified: EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink.swift 640/650/674 fire at persistent audition-sink init and on every default-output-device or sample-rate change (normal user workflow via AudioObjectAddPropertyListenerBlock at lines 679/699); AudioBackendSelection.swift:77 fires once per backend sample-rate resolution; RuntimeCMixerBackend.swift:1005 fires per runtime trace event but only when traceWriter.isEnabled (guard at RuntimeCMixerBackend.swift:2028-2030), so the highest-rate leak path is trace-gated diagnostics. One correction to the repro: the HAL may return the same cached CFString instance per device, so the bug can manifest as unbounded over-retain of a live object rather than distinct leaked allocations, and Instruments Leaks may not attribute it; Allocations/refcount tracking would. Ownership violation and memory growth are real either way. Fix is a one-token change to takeRetainedValue(). Severity LOW is correct (tiny strings, low frequency in normal use); neither inflated nor deflated. Not alpha-blocking.
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding is real exactly as described. stringProperty obtains a caller-owned (+1) CFString for kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceUID and bridges it with takeUnretainedValue() with no release, leaking one CFString per successful call (including the empty-string early-return path at lines 146-148). Normal-runtime leak rate is tiny: once at app launch via EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink.init -> installDefaultOutputListener (sink constructed unconditionally at AppDelegate.swift:165), once per default-output-device change (defaultOutputDidChange, line 640) or format change (outputFormatDidChange, line 650), and once per RuntimeCMixerSampleRateCandidates.current() during backend setup (AudioBackendSelection.swift:77). The higher-rate per-trace-event path (RuntimeCMixerBackend.swift:2063 via audioGraphDiagnostics at 1004-1005) is doubly gated: guard traceWriter.isEnabled at line 2028, and RuntimeCMixerTraceConfiguration.makeWriter is #if DEBUG (RuntimeCMixerDiagnostics.swift:1720-1733) so Release builds always get NoopRuntimeCMixerTraceWriter — the reporter's mitigation note is accurate. Correct fix is takeRetainedValue() (or explicit release). Severity LOW is correct: unambiguous Copy-rule violation but bounded to a few dozen bytes per rare occurrence in supported workflows; no state corruption, no crash risk. Refutation attempts failed: no compensating release exists anywhere in the file, the leak occurs precisely on the noErr success path, and the audition-sink call sites are not debug-gated.

**Independently rediscovered by:** `CS-offline-diag:cfstring-leak-device-uid-property` (LOW) — merged into this finding; concurrence across independent auditors raises confidence.

#### VTX-E-005 — Both CoreAudio output hosts pass Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) as the render-callback refCon and stop/dispose the AudioUnit inside deinit; a render callback di

- **ID:** VTX-E-005 (`E-memory-safety:unretained-refcon-deinit-race`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** Medium
- **Category:** callback-lifetime
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** Both CoreAudio output hosts pass Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) as the render-callback refCon and stop/dispose the AudioUnit inside deinit; a render callback dispatched in the window between the final strong release and AudioOutputUnitStop would takeUnretainedValue() (retain) an object whose deinit has begun.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink.swift: refCon at line 779, callback takeUnretainedValue at line 10, deinit stops/disposes at lines 583-593 (resetOutputUnit lines 810-818). app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/RuntimeCMixerBackend.swift: refCon at line 224, callback at lines 119-125, deinit -> reset() lines 141-143 and 283-297.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** An object must not be retained (resurrected) after its deinit has started; audio callbacks must never dereference a deallocating host.

**Why it matters:** Retain-during-deinit is undefined behavior in Swift; the window is a few instructions wide and requires a callback to fire exactly as the last owner releases the host on another thread, so practical risk is low, but on the audition sink the host is created/destroyed per editor lifecycle so the window recurs.

**Reproduction / proof:** Not practically reproducible on demand; the hazard is architectural. Proposed detection: TSan run while rapidly creating/destroying EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink instances under active audio output.

**Existing mitigation:** AudioOutputUnitStop inside deinit blocks until any in-flight render completes before the unit is disposed; both hosts are long-lived in normal use; the pattern matches common CoreAudio practice.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Add an explicit invalidate()/teardown method called while a strong reference still exists (before release), or pass a retained refCon whose lifetime is managed by the stop path, so the callback can never observe a deinit-ing host.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Thread Sanitizer soak creating/destroying the audition sink during playback; code review that no code path releases the last host reference while its unit is running.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability synthetic/noncanonical only, confidence High): The code pattern is exactly as reported: both CoreAudio hosts install Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) as the render refCon and stop/dispose the unit inside deinit, so a render callback firing between the final strong release and AudioOutputUnitStop would takeUnretainedValue() (transient ARC retain) on a deiniting object — a genuine latent Swift lifetime hazard, and the reporter's mitigations are also correct (deinit orders AudioOutputUnitStop before scratch deallocation, and Stop blocks until in-flight renders complete, so no use-after-free of memory; the residual issue is retain-during-deinit UB only). However, the reporter's reachability rationale is factually wrong: EditorNoteAuditionAudioSink is NOT created/destroyed per editor lifecycle — it is instantiated exactly once in AppDelegate.init, stored in a let property on an AppDelegate strongly retained for the whole process via static retainedDelegate, so its deinit never runs in the shipped app (macOS apps exit() without draining statics). The RuntimeCMixerAudioEngine/host pair is likewise a process-lifetime singleton (let audioEngine in PlaybackEngine, let playbackEngine on the immortal delegate). Host deinit is exercised only by unit tests. CONFIRM as latent architectural robustness debt (would silently arm if ownership ever becomes per-editor/per-document); severity LOW is appropriate, but reachability corrected from "supported user workflow" to synthetic-only at this commit. Reasonable eventual hardening: remove/nil the render callback (or use passRetained plus an explicit invalidate()) before the owner can release the host; no urgency for the alpha.

#### VTX-F-004 — Export progress updates are forwarded to the MainActor via independent unstructured Task creations from the render thread, which do not guarantee FIFO execution

- **ID:** VTX-F-004 (`F-concurrency-stale:progress-task-ordering-not-guaranteed`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** Medium
- **Category:** concurrency-ui
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** Export progress updates are forwarded to the MainActor via independent unstructured Task creations from the render thread, which do not guarantee FIFO execution, so progress text/bar can transiently regress or interleave across stage boundaries; a straggler progress Task also resolves self?.audioExportProgressSheet dynamically rather than the sheet it belongs to.

**Evidence:** AppDelegate.swift:578-582 and :632-636 (per-event Task { @MainActor } creation); completion Tasks at :583-585 and :637-639; stale-late-update safety exists only because finishWAVExport nils the slot (:590-591) before presenting alerts.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Progress presentation follows emitter order (WAVExportProgressEmitter emits monotonically; delivery may reorder).

**Why it matters:** Cosmetic UI wobble under scheduler contention; in the re-entry scenario it lets export A's straggler update export B's sheet, compounding the HIGH finding.

**Reproduction / proof:** Proposed: stress harness creating many MainActor Tasks from a background thread and recording arrival order; not deterministically reproducible in-app.

**Existing mitigation:** Emitter throttles to ~1% steps and forces stage transitions; the current runtime usually preserves creation order; slot nil-ing prevents post-completion updates.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Route progress through a single AsyncStream consumed by one MainActor task, or capture the specific sheet instance in the progress closure.

**Recommended timing:** post-v1

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Code inspection after refactor; long-export GUI smoke watching for percent regressions.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding confirmed exactly as described, at the reported LOW severity. (a) Progress events are forwarded from a background GCD thread via independent unstructured Task { @MainActor } creations; Swift specifies no execution order across independently created Tasks, and AudioExportProgressSheet.update/applyProgress has no monotonicity guard, so delivery reorder would visibly regress the bar/status text. Today's runtime effectively preserves enqueue order for equal-priority MainActor jobs and the emitter throttles to >=1% steps, so this is a rare, transient, cosmetic wobble — LOW, not higher. (b) The closure resolves self?.audioExportProgressSheet dynamically rather than capturing the sheet it belongs to (the progressSheet local is available at 562/616 but unused in the closure); combined with the export menu items NOT being gated on hasConflictingDocumentPresentation (validateMenuItem:230-233 -> WAVExportCoordinator.canExport:334-361 checks only document/playback state), a second export's sheet can receive the first export's updates — and export A's finish would close/nil export B's sheet. That compounding effect is real but is properly attributed to the separate re-entry finding; this finding stands on its own as LOW. (c) Completion Task is created after export() returns so all progress Tasks precede it in creation order; finishWAVExport/finishM4AExport nil the slot (590-591/644-645) making single-export stragglers no-op via optional chaining. Identical pattern exists for M4A (627-641). Fix is trivial: capture progressSheet in the closure and/or forward via a FIFO channel (DispatchQueue.main.async or one AsyncStream consumer).

First-party-by-tag is common accepted practice, so this is hardening rather than a demonstrated defect; the version skew (v5 vs v7) also suggests no single pinning policy.

All mitigation claims check out: secret steps gated on tag pushes (release.yml:47,141,166,174,188,194,208), keychain cleanup under always() (release.yml:219). Additional supporting detail the reporter did not cite: the Developer ID .p12 is written to $RUNNER_TEMP at release.yml:80 and only removed at release.yml:222, so the mutable-tag upload-artifact@v7 step (line 200) executes while the certificate file and unlocked keychain are on disk — the exfiltration path described is concrete, though it requires compromise of a GitHub-maintained action's tag. Severity LOW is correct: hardening/policy-consistency debt, not a demonstrated defect; reachability is CI-only. Fix is trivial (SHA-pin all four refs, align checkout versions).

#### VTX-I-002 — Container preflights bound memory (64 MiB mono cap) but not wall-clock time: chunk/metadata walks are O(fileSize) seek+read pairs with no overall file-size cap,

- **ID:** VTX-I-002 (`I-adversarial-input:import-preflight-unbounded-walltime-no-cancel`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** High
- **Category:** dos/resource-exhaustion
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** Container preflights bound memory (64 MiB mono cap) but not wall-clock time: chunk/metadata walks are O(fileSize) seek+read pairs with no overall file-size cap, and the import operation has no cancellation, so a pathological file (e.g., multi-GB WAV of millions of 0-byte chunks or FLAC with millions of 4-byte metadata blocks) leaves the sample-import operation stuck busy until the walk completes.

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/WAVSampleImportDecoder.swift:389-406 (per-chunk 8-byte read loop bounded only by declaredEnd<=fileSize); FLACSampleImportDecoder.swift:133-152 (metadata walk advances >=4 bytes/iteration, bounded only by fileSize); SampleEditorWAVImportCoordinator.swift:107-142 (Task.detached with no cancellation handle), 183-195 (operationToken blocks new imports while in flight), 224-235 (no cancel path).

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Hostile imported files must not be able to wedge the import subsystem.

**Why it matters:** A user opening a hostile 'sample pack' file from the internet gets a background task spinning for minutes with the importer locked (begin() refuses while operationToken is set); no crash or memory blowup, and the main thread stays responsive since work runs off-main.

**Reproduction / proof:** Craft a 2 GiB .wav: valid RIFF/WAVE header with declared size covering the file, then ~268M consecutive 8-byte chunk headers each declaring size 0 (any non-fmt/data id), ending with valid fmt+data chunks. Select it via Load Sample; preflight performs ~268M seek+read(8) pairs before completing, with no cancel affordance.

**Existing mitigation:** Frame-count cap (SampleImportResourcePolicy, WAVSampleImportDecoder.swift:48-64) bounds all allocations; walk terminates (strictly advancing offsets); work is off-main-thread; user must explicitly choose the file in an audio-filtered NSOpenPanel.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Add a sanity cap on preflight iterations or total container size for sample import (e.g., reject sources over a few hundred MB), and/or plumb Task cancellation from the coordinator into the preflight read loops.

**Recommended timing:** post-v1

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test with a generated many-chunk WAV asserting inspect() rejects it quickly under the new cap; manual check that cancel/second import works during a long-running import.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Finding is real as described. WAV preflight chunk walk and FLAC metadata walk are O(fileSize) seek+read syscall pairs with no overall file-size cap, no iteration cap, and no cancellation check; a crafted file of millions of 0-byte WAV chunks (8 bytes/iteration, up to ~536M iterations under the 32-bit RIFF size bound) or 0-length FLAC metadata blocks (4 bytes/iteration, file size wholly unbounded UInt64) keeps the detached inspection task busy for minutes. The coordinator serializes imports on operationToken and stores no task handle, so there is no cancel path and begin() refuses new imports until the walk finishes. Attempted refutations all failed: no hidden iteration cap, no upstream size check (container detect reads only 12 bytes), no cancellation propagation, no concurrent-import escape. Reporter's mitigations verified: frame-count cap bounds memory, walks strictly advance so they terminate, work is off-main (UI responsive), NSOpenPanel is audio-UTType-filtered requiring explicit user selection, and the wedge self-clears when the walk completes or on relaunch. Severity LOW is correct (no corruption, no data loss, no crash, no memory blowup; deliberate hostile-file selection required). Minor citation corrections: Task.detached wiring is SampleEditorWAVImportCoordinator.swift:114-134 (not 107-142); begin() token guard is 186-188. Cheap remediation: cap preflight iterations or total file size, and/or store the task handle with Task.checkCancellation in the walk loops plus a cancel affordance.

#### VTX-I-003 — WAV and AIFF preflights require the pad byte of an odd-sized final chunk to lie within the declared container size (paddedEnd <= declaredEnd), rejecting the fil

- **ID:** VTX-I-003 (`I-adversarial-input:wav-final-odd-chunk-pad-strictness`)
- **Severity:** LOW
- **Confidence:** Medium
- **Category:** robustness/format-compat
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** WAV and AIFF preflights require the pad byte of an odd-sized final chunk to lie within the declared container size (paddedEnd <= declaredEnd), rejecting the file as 'truncated' otherwise; real-world writers sometimes omit the final pad byte for a trailing odd chunk (reachable for 8-bit mono WAV where blockAlign=1 permits odd data sizes).

**Evidence:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/WAVSampleImportDecoder.swift:394-398 (paddedEnd = end + (size & 1); guard paddedEnd <= declaredEnd else throw .truncatedWAV) with line 437 allowing odd dataSize when blockAlign==1; AIFFSampleImportDecoder.swift:140-144 (same padded-end requirement).

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Supported classic sample files that mainstream tools accept should import.

**Why it matters:** An importer this strict will refuse some legitimately produced legacy 8-bit mono WAVs (odd sample count, writer omitted trailing pad and counted only real bytes in the RIFF size) that afplay/Audacity/AVFoundation accept; user sees 'incomplete or truncated'. Security posture is unaffected (strictness errs safe).

**Reproduction / proof:** Build an 8-bit mono PCM WAV with a 3-byte data chunk as the last chunk, no trailing pad byte, RIFF size counting only actual bytes; SampleImportDecoder().inspect throws .truncatedWAV while AVAudioFile opens the same file fine.

**Existing mitigation:** Only affects odd-sized trailing chunks (mostly 8-bit mono); most encoders write the pad byte; user gets a clear error rather than corruption.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Allow the final chunk's pad byte to be absent when end == declaredEnd (accept unpadded EOF for the last chunk only).

**Recommended timing:** post-v1

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** Unit test importing an unpadded odd-length trailing data-chunk WAV succeeds and decodes the expected frame count.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Traced and reproduced. WAV preflight chunk walk computes paddedEnd = end + (size & 1) and throws .truncatedWAV when paddedEnd > declaredEnd (WAVSampleImportDecoder.swift:392-398); validated() at line 437 permits odd dataSize when blockAlign==1 (8-bit mono), so an odd final data chunk is otherwise legal, but the padded-end guard fires first during the walk. AIFF has the symmetric guard throwing .truncatedAIFF (AIFFSampleImportDecoder.swift:140-144). Emulated the exact guard arithmetic in python3 against a synthesized 8-bit mono PCM WAV with a 3-byte trailing data chunk, no pad byte, RIFF size counting only real bytes: fmt chunk passes (paddedEnd 36 <= 47), data chunk fails (end 47 == declaredEnd 47, paddedEnd 48 > 47 -> truncatedWAV), while macOS AudioToolbox (afinfo, same CoreAudio backend AVAudioFile uses) opens the identical file fine as 3 frames of 8-bit mono. Reachable: AppDelegate.swift:39 wires SampleEditorWAVImportCoordinator with the live SampleImportDecoder; its flow calls inspect(url) before the channel prompt (SampleEditorWAVImportCoordinator.swift:136-139, 232), surfacing the 'incomplete or truncated' message. Correction to scope: the guard rejects ANY odd-sized trailing chunk whose pad byte is not counted in the RIFF size (e.g. odd trailing LIST/INFO text), not only 8-bit mono data chunks, so the affected population is slightly wider than the reporter framed. Fairness note limiting severity: pad-omitting files are technically non-conforming to RIFF/EA-IFF-85 word alignment, so this is real-world tolerance debt, not a spec violation by the importer; failure mode is a clear refusal with no corruption or security impact, and most encoders write the pad. LOW is the right severity; a targeted relaxation (accept end == declaredEnd for the final chunk, or clamp paddedEnd to declaredEnd when it is the last chunk) would fix it without weakening safety.

- **Category:** naming-consistency
- **Verification:** CONFIRMED by 1 independent adversarial verifier(s)

**Summary:** ApplicationMenuBuilder.Actions defines 22 menu selectors via NSSelectorFromString paired with @objc private methods on AppDelegate, so a method rename breaks the menu silently at runtime with no compile-time check.

**Evidence:** ApplicationMenuBuilder.swift 5-27 (22 NSSelectorFromString entries, e.g. 'playPressed:'); matching @objc private funcs in AppDelegate (playPressed 1914, duplicateSample 391, swapSample 435). validateMenuItem's default: returns true (AppDelegate 289-290), so an orphaned selector yields an enabled item that no-ops.

**Reachability:** supported user workflow

**Invariant affected:** Menu items dispatch to live handlers

**Why it matters:** Rename refactors (the exact cleanup this audit recommends elsewhere) can detach a menu item without any diagnostic; the pattern is repeated for every new command.

**Reproduction / proof:** Rename playPressed to playButtonPressed without touching ApplicationMenuBuilder; project compiles, Transport > Play stops working.

**Existing mitigation:** Actions are centralized in one enum and change rarely; menu-availability tests exercise validateMenuItem for most commands.

**Smallest recommended remediation (no implementation):** Make the handler methods internal @objc and reference them with #selector(AppDelegate.playPressed(_:)) from the builder, or add a debug-only assertion that AppDelegate responds(to:) every Actions selector at launch.

**Recommended timing:** beta hardening

**Suggested verification for a future fix:** A launch-time responds(to:) sweep over Actions asserts in tests.

**Adversarial verification notes:**
- *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability supported user workflow, confidence High): Core claim confirmed: 22 stringly-typed NSSelectorFromString actions with no compile-time or test-time check that AppDelegate implements them; a handler rename compiles clean and silently breaks the menu item. Two corrections to the reporter's evidence: (1) the failure mode is a DISABLED (grayed-out) item, not an enabled no-op — menu items carry an explicit target (ApplicationMenuBuilder.swift:243, build(target: self) at AppDelegate.swift:354) and the main menu keeps AppKit autoenablesItems=true (no override anywhere except Sample Editor destination pickers, SampleEditorWindowController.swift:179/296), so AppKit's responds-to-action check disables the item before validateMenuItem's default:true (AppDelegate.swift:289-290) is ever reached; (2) the reporter's mitigation claim is false — no test file references AppDelegate or validateMenuItem (grep of VoodooTrackerXTests returns zero hits); ApplicationMenuBuilderTests only asserts item.action == Actions.<x> (e.g. lines 122-126), which cannot detect a detached handler. I verified all 22 selector strings currently match an @objc private func in AppDelegate (no orphan exists today), so this is a latent maintainability hazard, not a present defect — LOW is the correct severity, not inflatable. Cheap hardenings: use #selector(AppDelegate.playPressed(_:)) (methods are already @objc) or add one test asserting AppDelegate.instancesRespond(to:) for every Actions constant.

(2) The reporter's 'CI checkout layout change' trigger is overstated: #filePath is baked at compile time and CI (.github/workflows/basic-checks.yml:20-39) builds and tests in the same checkout, so only repo-internal layout changes (test-file depth change within app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerXTests, or renaming tests/reference-xm) can break resolution — not where the repo is checked out. - *CONFIRMED* (verifier severity LOW, reachability build/CI only, confidence High): Core claim confirmed: referenceXMFixtureURL is privately duplicated 8x in the test target with divergent missing-fixture policies, and every copy climbs exactly 4 path components from #filePath to reach the repo root (correct today: repoRoot/app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerXTests/<File>.swift). ## Code-smell clusters (non-defect maintainability accumulations)

Clusters are reported per audit track; several tracks independently converged on the same accumulations (noted in the executive triage). Cluster entries retain their reporting track prefix.

#### Cluster `A1-lifecycle-model:hand-rolled-document-copy-constructors`

- **Severity:** medium
- **Files/symbols involved:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/BlankTrackerDocument.swift (mutators at 1364-1372, 1481-1494, 1503-1516, 1607-1620, 1634-1647, 1675-1688, 1716-1729, 1757-1770, 1797-1810, 1905-1918, 1933-1946, 1991-2004, 2111-2124, 2136-2149) vs replacingInstrumentPalette 1229-1246; parallel PlaybackInstrument full re-construction blocks in ~10 sites (PlaybackModel.swift has only withName)
- **What accumulated:** About fourteen near-identical 12-field BlankTrackerDocument memberwise copies inside mutating methods, only four of which use the replacingInstrumentPalette helper; plus repeated 7-field PlaybackInstrument re-construction wherever one field (samples or map) changes.
- **Why incremental PR history likely contributed:** Each sample-lifecycle PR (populate, clear, duplicate, permutation, metadata setters, order editing) added its own mutator copying the whole struct rather than extending a shared with()-style helper, because each PR was scoped to one operation under the <=500-line rule.
- **Current concrete cost/risk:** Adding any new document field (e.g., per-document octave, edit step) requires touching ~15 call sites; a missed site silently drops the new field to a stale value inside one specific operation, which snapshot-undo would then faithfully propagate. Same for PlaybackInstrument fields.
- **Smallest consolidation direction:** Introduce BlankTrackerDocument.with(selection:instrumentPalette:patterns:orderState:) and PlaybackInstrument.with(samples:noteSampleMap:name:) copy helpers and migrate mutators mechanically; pure refactor guarded by the existing exhaustive equality-based tests.
- **Why NOT to refactor now:** Behavior-neutral and fully test-covered, but it churns the exact files the Sample Lifecycle Alpha gate just froze; no active defect traced to it yet.
- **Recommended milestone:** beta hardening

#### Cluster `A1-lifecycle-model:duplicated-instrument-invariant-guard-chains`

- **Severity:** medium
- **Files/symbols involved:** BlankTrackerDocument.swift: selectedEmptySamplePopulationDestination 1083-1096, nextAppendSampleIndex 1121-1126, sampleDuplicationTarget 1421-1429, sampleSlotPermutationContext 1271-1281, plus EditableXMWriter.swift 293-315 re-deriving the same checks
- **What accumulated:** Five slightly different hand-inlined versions of the canonical-instrument validity predicate (indices in 0..<16, unique, complete samples, map nil-or-exact-96 with in-range entries). Each site includes a different subset: append omits map checks entirely, populate accepts nil map, duplicate/permutation require it, the writer re-implements all of it with throwing variants.
- **Why incremental PR history likely contributed:** Each lifecycle operation PR added its own guard chain tuned to its immediate test matrix instead of extracting a shared `canonicalInstrumentState(for:)` validator, keeping diffs small per PR.
- **Current concrete cost/risk:** Divergence is already observable (finding nil-map-populate-append-keeps-nil-map exists precisely because two of the five sites disagree about map presence); future operations will copy whichever neighbor chain is nearest, compounding drift.
- **Smallest consolidation direction:** Extract one `CanonicalInstrumentState` validator returning a typed struct (representedIndices, map, failures) consumed by populate/append/duplicate/permutation and by the writer's throwing path; encode the keymap-presence invariant in exactly one place.
- **Why NOT to refactor now:** Requires deciding the nil-map policy question first (finding above); refactoring before that decision would just freeze the current ambiguity.
- **Recommended milestone:** beta hardening (after resolving keymap-presence normalization)

#### Cluster `A1-lifecycle-model:blanktrackerdocument-file-grab-bag`

- **Severity:** low
- **Files/symbols involved:** app/VoodooTrackerX/VoodooTrackerX/BlankTrackerDocument.swift (2430 lines): TrackerNoteKeyMap 3-71, audition request/policy/previewer 148-727, DeterministicSampleGenerator 729-776, document model 832-2324, EditablePlaybackSongBuilder 2343-2410, control-panel metadata 2412-2430
- **What accumulated:** Six unrelated concerns (keyboard note mapping, audition routing policy, preview lifecycle, PCM generation, the canonical document model, playback snapshot building) share one file named for only one of them; the paired test file mirrors this at 5318 lines mixing model, previewer, mixer, and playback-engine tests.

- **What accumulated:** The 'can this lifecycle action run' predicate for each action is evaluated in three to four distinct formulations: display-state gate composition (six repeated !playing && !importing && !conflict conjunctions), per-action CommandAvailability enums, partially dead coordinator can-properties, and model-level validators — plus the six hand-listed mutual-exclusion sites.
- **Why incremental PR history likely contributed:** Gating style changed mid-chain: early PRs (sine, import) added coordinator can-properties; the clear PR introduced capture-based gating; duplicate/move/swap PRs introduced display-state CommandAvailability enums — each PR adopted the then-current style without retiring the prior one.
- **Current concrete cost/risk:** Readers cannot tell which gate is authoritative for a given entry point; policy changes (e.g. allowing an action during playback) require locating every formulation; dead properties invite fixing the wrong stack.
- **Smallest consolidation direction:** One availability function per action on a lifecycle facade, consumed by menu validation, button enablement, and begin-guards; delete the dead coordinator properties.
- **Why NOT to refactor now:** The defense-in-depth redundancy is currently harmless (model layer is authoritative) and the gate just certified the exact behavior; consolidation belongs with the coordinator-family refactor above.
- **Recommended milestone:** next milestone

## Security summary

| Area | Threat model | Current controls | Finding IDs | Residual risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| XM/MOD parsing (hostile module from the internet) | Crafted headers/counts/offsets → OOB read, overflow, exhaustion, silent mis-parse | C gate validates magic/header/pattern bounds; Swift walkers bound reads; event cap (2048/pattern) with warning field; ASan/UBSan harnesses in this audit found no memory-safety break | VTX-C1-001, VTX-C1-002, VTX-C1-003, VTX-C1-004, VTX-A1-003 | Moderate-low: no crash/exploit found; main exposure is silent partial/incorrect loads flowing into editable copy rather than memory unsafety |
| Audio import (hostile WAV/AIFF/FLAC) | Chunk-length lies, huge declared sizes, decoder disagreement | Container identity authoritative; STREAMINFO preflight; 64 MiB mono cap; depth allowlist; decode/preflight cross-check; background decode with revalidation | VTX-I-002, VTX-I-003 | Low: memory bounded; residual is wall-clock DoS on pathological files and over-strict rejects |
| File I/O / export ownership | Destination clobber, source-path claim, temp litter, symlink games | All three writers (XM/WAV/M4A) use temp-file + atomic replace; destination preserved on failure; no source-path ownership ever claimed (verified across coordinators) | VTX-F-003, VTX-F-001 | Low for data integrity (strong); residual is orphaned hidden temp files on quit/crash and the re-entry UI wedge |
| Private-data hygiene | Private module names/paths leaking into tracked files or releases | `scan-tracked-private-leaks.sh` in CI and run green here; docs discipline consistently observed (audit found no leak in any tracked file) | VTX-H-001 | Low-moderate: Release builds honor `VTX_*` env hooks incl. a WAV capture writer to arbitrary paths and auto-open/autoplay; local-attacker-only by nature but contradicts debug/release separation |
| CI / supply chain | Workflow compromise, tag-based action drift, token overreach, untested release artifacts | Minimal third-party actions (one SHA-pinned); no `pull_request_target`; secrets only in tag-gated release job; keychain cleanup `always()` | VTX-I-001, VTX-I-005, VTX-N-007, VTX-N-008 | Low: realistic exposure is process (untested tag → signed DMG) more than compromise |
| Runtime Swift/C boundary | UAF, double-free, overflow, index aliasing across the FFI | Value-snapshot plans; C copies PCM on add; status-code contracts; 256-slot fixed pool; audit harnesses + full trace found no UAF/double-free | VTX-E-001, VTX-E-003, VTX-E-004, VTX-E-005, VTX-E-002 | Low: contract edges and leaks, all currently guarded by caller discipline; no reachable memory corruption demonstrated |
| Async lifecycle (stale state) | Stale sheet/import/export commits against a changed document | Uniform Context/Capture pattern: documentIdentity + revision + selection captured and revalidated at every async boundary (a genuine strength — see positives) | VTX-A2-001, VTX-F-004 | Low: defense is consistent; residual is silent-discard UX, not wrong-document mutation |
| Asset provenance / licensing | Shipping assets the project lacks rights to redistribute | None for the icon (no attribution/provenance records) | VTX-CS-003, VTX-CS-006 | The one HIGH legal exposure; trivially remediable |

**Overall security conclusion:** for a local-first document app, the load-bearing boundaries
(parser bounds, export atomicity, private-data hygiene, stale-state defense) are in genuinely good
shape; adversarial passes designed to break them failed. The realistic risks found are operational
(Release env hooks, untested release tags, icon licensing), not memory-safety or data-corruption
exposures.


## Test-gap summary

**Inventory:** ~1,630 test functions across 26 Swift test files (per-file counts in the L-track
coverage notes), plus 222 Python tool tests. No sleeps, no `waitForExpectations`, no async-after
timing anywhere — brittle-timing risk is essentially zero, which is rare and worth preserving.

### High-value under-tested semantic chains

1. **AppDelegate glue (0 direct tests).** Every Sample Lifecycle gesture chain is tested from the
   coordinator inward; the menu→AppDelegate wiring (context builders, the six-site conflict matrix,
   selection mirrors) is enforced only by manual discipline
   (VTX-L-002, corroborated by the verifier trace on
   VTX-K-005).
2. **Viewport geometry via shadows.** The tests that exist validate drifted reimplementations
   (VTX-L-001); production selector labels, insets, and
   clip geometry have contradictory or absent coverage.
3. **Export re-entry and termination.** No test covers a second export started mid-export
   (VTX-F-001) or quit-during-export temp
   cleanup (VTX-F-003).
4. **Release-configuration behavior.** CI never builds Release; the optimizer workaround class of
   failure is historically demonstrated in this repo (VTX-N-001);
   the shipped x86_64 slice is never executed ({id:N-build-ci-release:x86_64-slice-never-tested}).
5. **Fxx/portamento reference parity.** The parity findings in this audit came from code reading,
   not from any failing test — deterministic reference-derived timing/pitch oracles for the effect
   engine are absent (see VTX-CS-001).

### Duplicated / low-value areas

- Eleven Test* shadow types in `TestSupport.swift` (four drifted) and a forked
  `PatternEditEngine` copy testing an unwired feature
  (VTX-L-003).
- Vacuous assertions: value-type "source unmutated" self-comparisons
  (VTX-CS-027,
  VTX-CS-013), a tautological gutter-alignment test
  (VTX-L-005), and two Python tests exercising
  only the stdlib (VTX-CS-019).
- Builder sprawl: 624 raw `PlaybackSample` constructions in 18 files; 41 per-file `make*` builders
  duplicating `TestSupport` (P cluster `test-scaffold-sprawl`).

### Release/toolchain-only gaps

Version stamping absent from released bundles, dSYMs not retained, Xcode version unpinned in both
workflows, and the `@_optimize(none)` workaround has no removal tracking
(VTX-N-005).

### Manual-only evidence that may deserve deterministic coverage later

The maintainer listening/UI checklist items (sheet parentage, red-close/Command-W router recreation,
preview/transport isolation, audible identity after lifecycle ops) are currently attestation-only.
The XCTSkip fixture-resolution policy (VTX-L-004) means
a resource-wiring regression would demote suites to silent green — worth a hard-fail in CI mode.

because it is absent**, and none of the audit's findings requires reversing a deferral.

## What is working unusually well

- **[A1-lifecycle-model]** SampleSlotPermutation transaction is genuinely atomic and algebraically sound: one validated bijection over the 16-slot domain (PlaybackModel.swift:451-517, move via remove/insert with correct destinationBySource inversion, swap, throwing domain validation) is applied in a single pass to represented sample identities, all 96 keymap entries, and the selection, then re-validated post-transform before a single whole-document assignment (BlankTrackerDocument.swift:1287-1342). No partial-application path exists; failure leaves the document bit-identical. Test coverage is exemplary: dense/sparse moves, represented-empty swap, move-to-S16, plus a 10-case noncanonical rejection matrix asserting zero mutation/revision/history (EditableDocumentEditCoordinatorTests.swift:532-959).
- **[A1-lifecycle-model]** Value-snapshot purity is real and actively enforced: every type inside a BlankTrackerDocument snapshot is a struct (PlaybackInstrument/PlaybackSample/envelopes, PlaybackModel.swift:28-448), tests assert no URL/source-path ownership can hide in the edit context via recursive Mirror inspection (EditableDocumentEditCoordinatorTests.swift:29-34, 1714-1720), and CoW sharing is verified down to the PCM buffer base address surviving an unrelated rename edit (line 997), keeping 20-level whole-document undo memory-cheap.
- **[A1-lifecycle-model]** Layered staleness protection around async/modal sample lifecycle operations: identity+revision+selection+content captures in the clear/move/swap coordinators (SampleEditorWindowController.swift:47-93, 359-404) sit on top of model-level re-validation (importAudioSample re-checks selectedSampleImportDestination == captured destination, BlankTrackerDocument.swift:1156-1162; addAudioSample re-checks live sample count, EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.swift:108-125), and blankDocument's didSet revision counter (AppDelegate.swift:16-18) invalidates any capture on any document reassignment.
- **[A1-lifecycle-model]** The edit coordinator's discipline is consistent: every lifecycle mutation funnels through one labeled applyEdit with no-op suppression (before != updated), reciprocal snapshot registration correct under isUndoing/isRedoing, and menu availability derived from the same model predicates the mutations use (EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.swift:42-64), eliminating a whole class of UI/model disagreement; coordinator tests verify undo/redo through real InstrumentEditor/SampleEditor window controllers, not just model equality.
- **[A2-lifecycle-ui-chain]** Uniform token+capture+revision stale-confirmation architecture across all four multi-turn lifecycle ops (Clear/Move/Swap/Import): every confirmation re-validates document identity (UUID), monotonic revision (bumped on every blankDocument assignment, AppDelegate.swift:16-18), selection, exact captured sample equality, and editable+stopped context; tests enumerate 8-9 distinct stale contexts per coordinator (SampleEditorWindowControllerTests.swift:1150-1211, 1263-1326, 1388-1473) and the deliberate own-sheet modal exception is commented and separately tested (SampleEditorWindowController.swift:77-79, 389-391; tests 1213-1233, 1328-1355).
- **[A2-lifecycle-ui-chain]** No enabled-state lies found: every displayState enable flag is derived from the same model predicate the commit path re-checks (isClearEnabled/representedSampleForClear, isMove/SwapEnabled/representedSampleForSlotPermutation incl. canonical 96-map, isDuplicateEnabled/sampleDuplicationTarget, isWAVLoadEnabled/selectedSampleImportDestination), giving 4-5 concentric validation layers (view guard -> AppDelegate wrapper -> coordinator capture -> BlankTrackerDocument transactional guard -> applyEdit no-op rejection) with zero divergence found between menu/button eligibility and model acceptance.
- **[A2-lifecycle-ui-chain]** Every sample lifecycle mutation routes through EditableDocumentEditCoordinator.applyEdit with reciprocal snapshot undo; selection changes are correctly non-undoable direct assignments (AppDelegate.swift:1831-1882) that still bump revision and thereby invalidate all in-flight captures — a clean two-tier state model.
- **[A2-lifecycle-ui-chain]** Stale-widget rigor: tests deliberately retain detached buttons after a full view rebuild and re-send their old target/action, asserting the current displayState guard (not widget enablement) is the authority (tests 324-371, 394-434) — this closes the classic AppKit stale-sender hole by construction (guards at SampleEditorWindowController.swift:1281, 1458, 1505, 1521).
- **[A2-lifecycle-ui-chain]** Async import pipeline is main-thread-clean and interleaving-safe: decode runs via Task.detached with a thread assertion test (1875-1898), every async resume re-checks operation token AND capture currency (including canAppendSample for add-as-new), and mutation provably cannot occur before the candidate completes (gate test 1837-1873).
- **[A2-lifecycle-ui-chain]** Preview/audition lifecycle is disciplined: audition auto-releases on window resign-key, window close, and any display-state change of source/instrument/slot/sample (SampleEditorWindowController.swift:1198-1226); import and sine commits explicitly cancel previews (AppDelegate.swift:1071, 1181); permutation/duplicate commits cancel via the selection-change hook in applyEditableDocumentSnapshot (1497-1499); token key-identity filtering prevents cross-editor visual confusion (1216-1219).
- **[A2-lifecycle-ui-chain]** The floating-panel-over-sheet z-order problem is solved explicitly (temporarily un-float, orderBack, restore with sheetParent/visibility guards) rather than accidentally, with the policy and presenter behavior pinned by tests (InstrumentEditorWindowController.swift:535-573; test 1961-1993).
- **[B-reference-integrity]** Stable sample identity is carried as PlaybackSample.sampleIndex (never array position) end-to-end: every lookup goes through identity search (PlaybackInstrument.sample(mappedSampleIndex:) PlaybackModel.swift:438-447, keymap resolver :629-664, writer's Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:) keyed by sampleIndex EditableXMWriter.swift:342-349, editor mutations via firstIndex(where: $0.sampleIndex == ...) BlankTrackerDocument.swift:1656-1658). I found zero sites that index a samples array positionally with a keymap or slot value.
- **[B-reference-integrity]** The 1-based-UI / 0-based-internal boundary is crossed exactly once per surface and then double-checked: UI handlers convert slot-1 (InstrumentEditorWindowController.swift:2288-2291 etc., AppDelegate.swift:398-399), and the document layer independently re-derives the same identity from selection and rejects mismatches (duplicateSample/clearSample/permutation guards, BlankTrackerDocument.swift:1408-1434, 1436-1452, 1259-1283). This double-entry bookkeeping makes off-by-one drift structurally detectable.
- **[B-reference-integrity]** Transactional capture/confirm pattern for Clear/Move/Swap/Import is genuinely robust: captures pin document identity UUID + monotonically bumped revision (AppDelegate.swift:14-18 didSet) + exact source PlaybackSample value + exact noteSampleMap, and re-validate all of it at confirm (SampleEditorWindowController.swift:47-93, 359-404; SampleEditorWAVImportCoordinator.swift:73-105). Stale-destination commits are effectively impossible.
- **[B-reference-integrity]** First-playable fallback is strictly quarantined: the canonical resolver defaults to .fail (PlaybackModel.swift:611-664); .firstPlayableSample appears only in the legacy AVAudio trigger path (PlaybackEngine.swift:1655-1659) and in the runtime adapter's nil-keymap branch where it is explicitly counted and surfaced as diagnostics (PlaybackSongAdapter+Diagnostics.swift:670-752, firstPlayableSampleFallbackUsed). Editable-document audition and playback stay keymap-/direct-selection-driven.
- **[B-reference-integrity]** Writer/reopen canonical-empty round-trip is exact by construction: XMSampleExport.canonicalEmptySlot emits 40 zero bytes with declared header size 40 (EditableXMWriter.swift:527-538, 638, 683-694), and PlaybackSongBuilder detects exactly declaredSampleHeaderSize == 40 && all-zero (PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:194-199); provenance-gated Make Editable Copy refuses to guess at anything else, with dry-run writer validation before adopting the copy (LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator.swift:151-156).
- **[B-reference-integrity]** SampleSlotPermutation is a small, closed algebra (validated total permutation over 0..<16 with inverse, PlaybackModel.swift:451-517) and applySampleSlotPermutation revalidates the entire post-image (unique indices, complete samples, 96-entry in-range map, selection) before committing atomically (BlankTrackerDocument.swift:1286-1342).
- **[C1-xm-parser]** C parser hostile-input robustness is genuinely strong: I ran ~760k mutation and truncation fuzz iterations under ASan+UBSan against mc_parse_xm_header_bytes and mc_parse_mod_header_bytes (seeds: tests/fixtures/minimal.xm, minimal.mod, and two generated instrument fixtures) with zero memory or UB reports; the strict full-consumption check (xm_header.c:280-282), explicit ceilings (channels<=64, patterns<=256, rows 1-256 at xm_header.c:151-156,214), and the 32-bit SIZE_MAX overflow guard (xm_header.c:135) all held under adversarial input.
- **[C1-xm-parser]** Hostile-input regression tests exist and are specific: tests/core/ModuleCoreTests.swift:99-225 covers truncated declared header, zero/excessive channels, excessive patterns, zero/excessive pattern rows, truncated pattern header, truncated packed data, and order-table clamping when the header ends early — unusual discipline for an alpha-stage parser, backed by golden JSON snapshots.
- **[C1-xm-parser]** Writer/parser symmetry for the canonical 40-byte all-zero empty-slot placeholder is exact and independently re-verified at three layers: EditableXMWriter emits declared sample header size 40 and an all-zero placeholder (EditableXMWriter.swift:92,527-538,638,683-694), PlaybackSongBuilder detects exactly that shape (PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:196-199), and LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator.matchesLoadedSampleCopyBoundary re-checks span exactness before allowing a copy (lines 159-201).
- **[C1-xm-parser]** Keymap-driven sample resolution is value-matched rather than index-based (PlaybackModel.swift:438-440 samples.first { $0.sampleIndex == mappedSampleIndex }), so hostile note-sample-map bytes (0-255 raw from file, PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:248-261) can never index out of bounds — they simply resolve to silence.
- **[C1-xm-parser]** Sample loop metadata from hostile headers is clamped safely into [0, length] before reaching the mixer (PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:393-408 safeLoopStartInSamples/safeLoopLengthInSamples), covering the classic loop-start+length-beyond-data attack.
- **[C1-xm-parser]** The synthetic fixture pipeline is exemplary: deterministic hash-pinned outputs, strict schema validation with representable-range checks (scripts/generate-synthetic-xm-fixtures.py:54-261), path-traversal confinement (resolved_child, lines 505-513), and dedicated tests for determinism, private-path leak prevention, and output confinement (tools/synthetic_xm_fixture_generator_tests.py:94-160,312-354,427-452).
- **[C2-xm-writer-copy]** Byte-golden regression locking: testDenseAlpha1OutputRemainsByteIdentical (EditableXMWriterTests.swift:1139-1163) pins a SHA-256 of dense alpha.1 output, and multiple tests assert double-invocation byte equality (e.g. :967-968, :1313-1314, :1563-1564), making writer determinism and format drift immediately detectable.
- **[C2-xm-writer-copy]** Exact provenance-based canonical-empty acceptance: XMSourceSampleSlotProvenance records decoded payload length plus a strict 'declared header size == 40 and all 40 bytes zero' predicate (PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:194-199), and matchesLoadedSampleCopyBoundary (LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinator.swift:161-202) demands exact span coverage — verified by a negative mutation matrix over name/volume/panning/reserved/trailing bytes (LoadedModuleEditableCopyCoordinatorTests.swift:802-855). This is a well-engineered, falsifiable boundary rather than heuristic acceptance.
- **[C2-xm-writer-copy]** PCM round-trip is provably lossless: import canonicalizes onto the 16-bit grid (WAVSampleImportDecoder.swift:167 via XMPCMQuantizer.signed16/canonicalFloat32), writer quantizes with the same /128 and /32768 conventions the reader uses (EditableXMWriter.swift:36-54, PlaybackSongBuilder.swift:437-459), and delta encode/decode are exact mod-2^n inverses, so reopened PCM equals in-memory PCM exactly (asserted with XCTAssertEqual on Float arrays).
- **[C2-xm-writer-copy]** Writer error surface is typed and precise (EditableXMWriterError carries instrument/sample indices and offending values, EditableXMWriter.swift:57-82), the export coordinator maps failures to distinct user-facing categories without touching the destination, and ExportXMCoordinatorTests verify existing-destination byte preservation on both writer and file-write failures.
- **[C2-xm-writer-copy]** The Sample Lifecycle milestone gate test (EditableXMWriterTests.swift:1406-1616) composes clear/move/duplicate/populate/swap with undo-redo, then chains export -> byte-identical re-export -> reopen -> provenance check -> Make Editable Copy -> byte-identical re-export — an end-to-end invariant net that would catch most regressions in this track in one place.
- **[C2-xm-writer-copy]** Intentional compatibility posture is documented: docs/format-changes.md precisely describes the sparse-slot span rule, canonical placeholder bytes, and the deliberate refusal to silently canonicalize noncanonical zero-length headers, matching the implemented code and tests line for line.
- **[CS-adapter-core]** Amiga period fidelity is verified bit-exact: xmAmigaPeriodLookup (PlaybackSongAdapter+RuntimeEvents.swift:489-610) matches ft2-clone's amigaPeriodLUT for all 1,920 reachable entries including FT2's quirky garbage final entry (22 at index 1919), and amigaPeriodFromLookup (line 612-619) reproduces FT2's exact indexing formula ((note-1)*16 + (finetune>>3)+16) with correct arithmetic-shift finetune quantization; C-4 anchors at 6848 as documented.
- **[CS-adapter-core]** The linear-frequency path (linearPitchTarget, PlaybackSongAdapter+RuntimeEvents.swift:372-418) implements FT2's period formula 7680 - 64*noteIndex - finetune/2 with the correct C-4 = period 4608 anchor, and every numeric path (playbackStep, floorFrame, clampedGain, fadeoutFrameDecrement) defensively guards non-finite/overflow inputs, so hostile module data cannot produce NaN/Inf frames or steps.
- **[CS-adapter-core]** PlaybackSongTraversalPlanner is fully bounded against hostile order tables: a derived row limit (16x selected rows, capped at 1M), a visited-position cycle guard for Bxx/Dxx backjumps, and per-channel E6x loop counters mean a malicious or looping module cannot hang or OOM the offline planner, with every truncation surfaced as an explicit diagnostic with a policy string.
