## Incremental-PR congestion assessment (Track P)

> If you did not know the PR history and only saw the repository today, where would you conclude
> incremental feature slices accumulated local complexity?

Answering that question cold, the five places a fresh reviewer would point at are:

1. **The lifecycle coordinator family** — Clear/Move/Swap are four-plus near-identical
   Context/Capture/Coordinator triples; Move vs Swap is a five-layer near byte-level clone (PR #388
   vs #389). A fresh reader assumes a shared abstraction exists and finds none.
2. **The mutual-exclusion matrix** — six `AppDelegate` sites each hand-enumerate the other
   coordinators' active flags; the display-state gate composes the same conjunction a seventh way.
   Omission compiles silently and no test covers the wiring.
3. **`AppDelegate.swift` and `BlankTrackerDocument.swift`** as accretion points — 117 and 53
   commits respectively; the document model file carries 14 inline memberwise reconstructions and a
   mid-chain helper adopted only by its 4 newest call sites, a visible strata line of PR history.
4. **The availability-predicate scatter** — per-action availability is evaluated in three to four
   distinct formulations (display-state conjunctions, CommandAvailability enums, partially dead
   coordinator `can*` properties VTX-P-003, model
   validators).
5. **Documentation accretion** — `docs/agent-current-state.md`'s 298-line chronological prose
   block, two parallel ~1,000-line roadmaps, and stale claims in README/design docs
   (VTX-O1-003 et al.) mean the
   fastest way to learn current truth is now reading code, which defeats the docs' purpose.

**Materiality verdict:** material and worth a scheduled consolidation milestone (see executive
triage), but *managed* — the same incremental process also produced the uniformly strong
stale-capture defense and the one-transaction permutation model, and no congestion cluster
currently causes a reachable defect.

  extension histograms, and per-directory counts; per-track file assignments were derived from that
  index so that every tracked file was owned by at least one auditor.
- **Directories reviewed:** `app/` (92 files), `core/` (9), `tests/` (15), `tools/` (9),
  `scripts/` (20), `docs/` (59), `.github/` (2), `assets/` (12), plus root metadata
  (`Package.swift`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`).
- **Read in full:** 207 of 224 tracked files were read end-to-end by at least one specialist
  auditor (per-track `readFully` lists retained in audit working data), including every Swift
  production file, every Swift test file, all C sources/headers, all Python scripts and tool tests,
  every workflow/config file, and all current docs/ADRs/design documents. The orchestrating
  reviewer additionally read `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, both GitHub workflow files,
  `ModuleCoreBridge.h`, and the two gate reports directly.
- **Opaque/binary files not semantically inspected** (inspected via metadata, hashes, generators,
  and consumers instead, per charter): `assets/logo/*.png`, `assets/logo/vtx-logo.svg`

  `tests/golden/*.json` (parsed and cross-checked), `tests/reference-xm/generated/*.xm` (verified

  finding is code-traced with an exact manual reproduction script instead), and the universal
  Release build duplication (cited from the internal gate per charter).


## Method appendix

The audit ran as an orchestrated multi-agent workflow at the audited commit:

1. **Track specialists (20):** tracks A (lifecycle model + UI chain, split), B (reference
   integrity), C (parser + writer/editable-copy, split), D (runtime C-mixer + preview/transport,
   split), E (Swift/C memory safety), F (concurrency/stale state), G (mutation defense in depth),
   H (path/export security), I (adversarial input + supply chain), J (architecture drift),
   K (code smells), L (test architecture), M (UI/AppKit), N (build/CI/release), O (governance +
   design docs, split), P (incremental-PR congestion). Each received an assigned full-read file
   list plus license to trace across boundaries.
2. **Coverage sweeps (18):** every tracked file not centrally assigned to a specialist was
   assigned to a sweep agent with an all-purpose defect lens, guaranteeing whole-repository
   coverage; a dedicated binary-inventory agent handled opaque files via metadata/consumers.
3. **Adversarial verification:** every material finding was re-examined by independent verifier
   agents instructed to refute it (BLOCKER/HIGH: 3 lenses — refute-with-code-trace,
   reproduce-or-bound-reachability, severity-calibration; MEDIUM: 1–2; LOW: 1). Verifier verdicts,
   calibrated severities, and notes are embedded per finding. Verifier-unanimous calibrations
   override reporter severities in the counts.
4. **Deduplication:** 17 independent rediscoveries were merged into primaries with provenance
   retained — cross-track concurrence is recorded as confidence evidence rather than double-counted.

Limitations: verifier coverage is 1–3 passes per finding, not exhaustive; UI findings are
code-traced rather than GUI-reproduced; line numbers cite the audited commit and will drift.
